title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's royal 'rupture' caused 'very serious damage' to the monarchy: author
summary: Royal commentators debate whether Meghan Markle could have succeeded in the royal family as the duchess celebrates her 45th birthday amid an unhealed rift.
story: Catherine Mayer, author of "Divide & Rule," explains why Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's departure from royal life dealt a lasting blow to the monarchy and its connection with younger audiences.
As Meghan Markle celebrates her 45th birthday, one royal author argues the Duchess of Sussex's exit from royal life caused "very serious damage" to the monarchy.

"I believe that the rupture in the family that saw Meghan and Harry go to the United States has done very serious damage to the monarchy," Catherine Mayer, who penned "Divide & Rule," told Fox News Digital.

"But to say that is not to say that I blame them for what happened," she said. "It's often taken as a criticism: 'Look what they've done to the monarchy.' I think this has been very painful for everybody and for the institution, but you need only look at the latest polling on the popularity of the monarchy to see that it is losing ground."
PRINCE HARRY LONGS FOR HIS OLD ROYAL LIFE AS AMERICA ISN'T WHAT HE EXPECTED, EXPERTS SAY

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex speaks onstage during the 2025 TIME100 Summit at Jazz at Lincoln Center on April 23, 2025, in New York City. The "Suits" alum's birthday is Aug. 4. (Jemal Countess/Getty Images for TIME)

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as senior royals in 2020, citing intrusive British media coverage and a lack of support from the palace. After moving to California, they aired their grievances in interviews and documentaries. Harry's 2023 memoir, "Spare," further strained his relationship with the family.

In July, the former American actress had planned to accompany her husband during several engagements on his return to the U.K. However, security concerns prevented Meghan and their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, from making the full trip.
"Divide & Rule" by Catherine Mayer is out now. (HQ)
While the Sussexes had a private meeting with King Charles and Queen Camilla on July 10, marking the first time since 2022 that Meghan had returned to England, she didn't make any public appearances.
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE'S EXIT HURT THE MONARCHY: AUTHOR
The couple lost their taxpayer-funded security when they stepped down as working royals. The Duke of Sussex has long sought to have it reinstated, citing concerns for his family's safety.

Mayer argued that, according to U.K. polls, the royal family has lost popularity primarily due to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, who was stripped of his princely title following his controversial relationship with late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. However, she believes that "undoubtedly," the Sussexes had an ability to connect with younger populations in a way that’s "not really there with the rest of the family."
Office workers in London watch the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's "Harry & Meghan" docuseries on Netflix on Thursday, Dec. 8, 2022. (Jonathan Brady/PA Images via Getty Images)
"The only ones who can potentially do it are Kate and William, and they're more of a small 'c' conservative in their approach," said Mayer, referring to the Prince and Princess of Wales.

Prince William, Prince of Wales, Catherine, Princess of Wales, Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex leave after escorting Queen Elizabeth II's coffin to Westminster Hall from Buckingham Palace for her lying in state on Sept. 14, 2022, in London. (Emilio Morenatti - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"They're young, but they're in their 40s," she said. "Their children are really young. And there's nobody in between George and his parents, William and Kate, to capture the imagination of younger audiences. Harry and Meghan are basically the same age, but they had this appeal, a much broader appeal, and that's been lost now."
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner echoed that view, noting that family divisions remain unresolved despite recent signs of reconciliation.

Prince Harry and actress Meghan Markle pose during an official photocall to announce their engagement at The Sunken Gardens at Kensington Palace in London, England, on Nov. 27, 2017. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"I feel there are major cracks in the royal family over Meghan and Harry, especially between King Charles and Prince William, who I believe are at loggerheads over the couple, culminating in the recent private meeting at Highgrove, leaving William blindsided about the meeting. Now, with Harry able to use Buckingham Palace again when he returns, it could be a breakthrough for Meghan and a heart-piercing wound for William."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, meets volunteer first responders from Bondi Surf Bathers' Life Saving Club during a visit to Bondi Beach on Day 4 of the royal trip to Australia on April 17, 2026, in Sydney. (Jonathan Brady-Pool/Getty Images)

While Meghan's relationship with King Charles reportedly softened following their private family reunion this summer, multiple reports continue to describe her ties with William and Kate as distant, with little evidence the broader royal rift has fully healed.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle take photographs with patients while visiting The Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne on April 14, 2026. (Joe Armao/The Age via Getty Images)

"In my book, I also examine the bullying allegations made against Meghan," said Mayer. "One of the problems was that they surfaced at exactly the time of the 2021 Oprah Winfrey interview. I think that made a lot of people suspect this was done to undercut anything Meghan might say in the interview. I'd actually been hearing about friction in the palace for a very long time before the story surfaced. As I explain in the book, that doesn't necessarily mean we're talking about bullying, but we're definitely talking about real friction there."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex attend The Endeavour Fund Awards at Mansion House in London on March 5, 2020. Soon after, they moved to California. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"We're talking about people who were very bruised by the experience, which includes her as well," Mayer continued. "But the fact is, there were real frictions between the brothers, William and Harry, as well as between the women and within the palace system. I don't think Meghan really understood that the monarchy will always give preference to the monarch and the immediate heir. And its members get very nervous when somebody feels bigger and more glamorous than the institution."
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex launches the Smart Works capsule collection on Sept. 12, 2019, in London, England. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
"The last thing they wanted to do was make her into some big star," Mayer added.
Turner noted that Meghan hasn't been the only one to experience struggles with "The Firm."
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex arrives for The Paley Center for Media gala honoring actor and director Tyler Perry at the Beverly Wilshire Hotel on Dec. 4, 2024. (AFP via Getty Images)

"Outsiders are accepted, provided they do not become more powerful or overshadow family members," he said. "In my time, Charles used to hate being overshadowed by Princess Diana at walkabouts. I believe this was part of the reason for the breakup. I feel palace employees and members of the royal family could see Meghan's charm was making her into another Diana in waiting."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Britain's Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, leave St. George's Chapel at Windsor Castle on May 19, 2018. (Ben Stansall - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Still, British royal expert Hilary Fordwich said mistakes made by the Sussexes cannot be overlooked and have contributed to their estrangement from the royal family.

"Harry and Meghan didn't just make a silly mistake," Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "They have undertaken a fundamentally damaging, deliberate strategy to undermine the royals, which is unforgivable. The Firm was most welcoming to her, bent the rules for her, made exceptions for her, but she thwarted it all. She didn't want to either learn or accept advice. King Charles and Prince William now have a narrower, more disciplined monarchy as a result."
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, arrive to attend the annual Commonwealth Day Service at Westminster Abbey in London on March 9, 2020. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)
"Yes, things could have been very different if Meghan had been dedicated to duty and not to herself and her own aggrandizement," said Fordwich.
Meghan Markle is seen here being interviewed by Oprah Winfrey on March 8, 2021. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard also told Fox News Digital that the secret to being a successful member of the British royal family is to adapt quickly.

"The House of Windsor may appear rigid, but it has run like clockwork and survived through history," said Chard. "The one thing people marrying into The Firm have to learn is to adapt. Both Princess Catherine and Meghan came in as outsiders. But one chose to learn the institution. The system is tough, but the system also gave Meghan support. The system can't save someone who won't play ball. The institution expects sacrifice before platform."

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attends an Invictus Games Friends and Family reception hosted by the City of The Hague and the Dutch Ministry of Defence at Zuiderpark on April 15, 2022, in The Hague, Netherlands. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
"Harry himself also talked about leaving royal life for years. Meghan gave him that push. Better handling could have delayed it, but I don't think it would have prevented it."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duke and Duchess of Sussex, leave a service of thanksgiving for the reign of Queen Elizabeth II at St. Paul's Cathedral in London on June 3, 2022, during Platinum Jubilee celebrations marking the monarch's 70 years of service. (Matt Dunham - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Mayer pointed out that Meghan was facing an uphill battle from the very beginning.

"When I was writing this book, I really did go back and challenge my own assumptions about whether Meghan could have ever made a go of it," said Mayer. "And I concluded that it was highly unlikely, and not her fault — or certainly not entirely her fault. One of the things people always say to me is, 'Of course she Googled Harry before they started dating. Of course, she knew about it.'"
Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, attends the Balenciaga Womenswear Spring/Summer 2026 show during Paris Fashion Week on Oct. 4, 2025, in Paris, France. (Getty Images for Balenciaga)

"I've been covering the monarchy for a very long time. I'm also the biographer of Charles, the man who is now King. I've spent a lot of time behind the scenes. Even after all the time I've spent there, I'm still surprised by the strangeness of the culture and how unlike any other culture it is."

From left: Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Prince William and Princess Catherine watch a Royal Air Force flypast from the balcony of Buckingham Palace on July 10, 2018, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

Mayer also recalled when Meghan received criticism for mimicking how she curtsied to the late Queen Elizabeth II in the Netflix docuseries "Harry & Meghan." However, audiences missed the point, she said.

"How weird it is to have a family where, even in private, you not only curtsy to the monarch, but you also follow an order of precedence," said Mayer. "How would anybody be prepared for that? The monarchy is essentially a medieval institution with some modern features grafted onto it."
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex attends the 2026 Fifteen Percent Pledge Fundraising Gala at Paramount Studios on Feb. 7, 2026, in Los Angeles. (Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)

Chard said "the damage has been done" following Meghan and Harry's departure. She noted the royal family has "moved on," prioritizing the future. While there will always be hope for reconciliation, she said, it will take time on all sides.
"Trust takes years to rebuild," she said.
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Emily Ratajkowski turns heads in bikini-filled July photo dump
summary: Emily Ratajkowski's July Instagram carousel features bikini photos and a mysterious moment holding an unidentified companion's bandaged hand.
story: Supermodel Emily Ratajkowski is getting backlash for an essay she wrote for The Cut, where she details her dating life after her divorce and life as as single mother.
Emily Ratajkowski is looking back on a month filled with sunshine, swimsuits and seaside views.
The 35-year-old model shared a carousel of photos from her summer travels on Instagram, captioning the post, "julio/Ιούλιος/july," writing the month in Spanish, Greek and English.
Among the snapshots was a close-up selfie of Ratajkowski wearing a navy blue bikini covered in white polka dots inside a coastal home.
Emily Ratajkowski shared a glimpse of her July travels with a polka-dot bikini selfie. (Emily Ratajkowski/Instagram)

The halter-style swimsuit featured thin straps that crossed around her waist, while her long brunette hair fell loosely over her shoulders. She looked directly into the camera with open shelves, glassware and blue cabinetry visible behind her.
The model's beach attire included an orange-and-black patterned bikini worn during a day by the water.
Emily Ratajkowski enjoyed a beachside afternoon while reflecting on her July travels. (Emily Ratajkowski/Instagram)

Sitting on a lounge chair covered with a yellow-and-white striped towel, Ratajkowski held a pink beverage in a glass beneath an oversized black-and-white umbrella. She accessorized the wraparound bikini with layered necklaces and several gold bangles.
A second image from the same setting showed the model turning the camera on herself.

Ratajkowski held her phone at arm’s length while seated sideways on the lounge chair, with rows of beach chairs and a glimpse of the water surrounding her. The late-day sunlight illuminated the scene as she appeared to check her reflection on the screen.
The carousel also included a quieter moment from an oceanfront dinner.

Wearing a dark brown halter top, Ratajkowski posed at a table overlooking the water as the sun set behind a row of trees. A cocktail, green drinking glass and place settings rested on the white tablecloth.
The model reached across the table to hold the bandaged hand of an unidentified companion. She did not identify the person or explain the apparent injury.
Emily Ratajkowski shared a quiet dinner moment overlooking the water during her July travels. (Emily Ratajkowski/Instagram)
Her summer photo album comes weeks after Ratajkowski reflected on the collapse of her marriage to film producer Sebastian Bear-McClard and the complicated period that followed.

The former couple married in 2018 and welcomed their son, Sylvester "Sly" Apollo, in March 2021. Ratajkowski filed for divorce in September 2022 and has since spoken openly about raising the 5-year-old primarily as a single mother in New York City.
In a June essay for The Cut titled "Mother F---er," Ratajkowski wrote that becoming a mother marked an abrupt shift in her identity before her marriage began to unravel.
"And then, in a time period that felt both instant and excruciatingly slow, my marriage collapsed," she wrote.
Ratajkowski admitted that she had feared becoming a single mother long before she had a child of her own.
"Even as a kid, I reasoned that of all the things I could grow up to be, it was crucial to avoid becoming a single mom," she wrote. "The term itself could be lodged as an insult."

As she navigated her divorce from Sebastian Bear-McClard, Emily Ratajkowski said she gradually recognized that leaving her marriage required courage and forced her to redefine her sense of self. (Allen Berezovsky/Getty Images)
Following the separation, the model threw herself into dating while attempting to reconcile her new reality with the way she believed others viewed her.
Despite the late nights, Ratajkowski said she established firm boundaries to protect her time with Sylvester.
"I had rules: Never miss bedtime and basically no sleepovers," she wrote. "These were natural and easy to abide by."
The model explained that she would return home regardless of how late a date ended, so she could be there when her son woke up.

"There was nowhere I’d rather be than when I woke up with my toddler, so no matter the number of martinis, I’d be fully dressed and out the door to relieve the sitter and be ready for my son’s 6 a.m. ‘Maamaaaa!’"
Although much of the essay detailed her post-divorce dating experiences, Ratajkowski said her most important realization came during a visit to her attorney’s office.
She recalled the lawyer telling her about women who remained in harmful marriages despite preparing to leave.
Emily Ratajkowski has one son, Sylvester Apollo Bear, who is 5. (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)
"You should be proud of yourself," he told her. "Most women don’t leave."
Ratajkowski said the conversation gave her a new understanding of the choice she had made.
"Leaving my marriage wasn’t about seeking anyone’s attention or approval," she wrote. "It was the opposite."
The model acknowledged that becoming a single mother changed the way others perceived her but ultimately helped her recognize her own strength.
"I wasn’t left; I left," she wrote. "I knew then that being able to leave, to say ‘no,’ was the only real superpower I’d gained through divorce. I was brave. Really, actually brave."

The essay sparked mixed reactions online. While some social media users criticized Ratajkowski as being out of touch with the realities facing many single mothers, others praised her for candidly discussing divorce, dating and motherhood.
Away from her personal life, Ratajkowski has continued expanding her fashion career.
Ratajkowski left acting behind because she felt like "a piece of meat." (Michael Simon/Getty Images for Primark)
She was recently announced as one of the faces of Abercrombie & Fitch’s fall 2026 denim campaign alongside model Paloma Elsesser and New York Giants players Jaxson Dart and Malik Nabers.
Speaking with Elle magazine about the campaign, Ratajkowski said she has become less concerned with following every fashion trend.
"I care less about trends and more about how clothes make me feel," she told the outlet. "I want pieces that fit into my life and make me feel like myself."
The New York-based model also explained why the city continues to shape her personal style.

"New York has always been my favorite city to get dressed in because everyone is aware they’re being perceived but also have the realities of their days to combat," she said. "There’s something incredibly stylish about practicality mixed with individuality."

Sarah Sotoodeh is an associate entertainment editor for Fox News Digital. She graduated from the University of Southern California with a Master’s Degree in Broadcast Journalism, and a Bachelor’s Degree in Biology from St. Edward’s University.

title: Spencer Pratt slams Ben Affleck's resurfaced claim that 'the cure for addiction is suffering'
summary: Spencer Pratt challenged Ben Affleck's claim that suffering cures addiction, inviting the actor to visit Skid Row and witness LA's drug crisis firsthand.
story: Los Angeles mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt outlines his approach to the homelessness crisis while speaking to local ABC reporter Josh Haskell.
Spencer Pratt called out Ben Affleck over past comments that the actor made about addiction and recovery.

In a resurfaced clip from Affleck's 2021 appearance on "The Howard Stern Show," the 53-year-old Oscar winner, who has publicly battled alcoholism for years, reflected on his own sobriety journey and argued that the "cure for addiction is suffering."

"I hate to say it, but the cure for addiction, the only cure I've seen, and not like these f------ overpriced rehabs or a lot of these fraudulent fixes that are sold to people. And they're good people who will support you. Alcoholics Anonymous, I think by and large, is a good organization. It's not the only one. The cure for addiction is suffering," Affleck said.
Spencer Pratt blasted Ben Affleck's past comments about the "cure for addiction." (Roy Rochlin/Getty Images; PG/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)

"You suffer enough that something inside you goes, ‘I’m done,'" he continued. "And I'm lucky because I hit that point where I lost really the things that were the most important. It was not my career or money. It was my relationship with my kids."

"And what I felt as if it impacted them," Affleck said. "I recognized it. It was the worst day of my life. I made amends. And for a while I thought, ‘Maybe this is temporary, maybe this feeling is going to go away.’ But since that day, I swear to Christ, I have not ever wanted to drink once."

On Monday, Pratt, a former Los Angeles mayoral candidate who made the city's addiction crisis one of his signature campaign issues, reposted the clip along with a blistering criticism of Affleck's viewpoint.
WHY SPENCER PRATT’S LOS ANGELES CAMPAIGN HAS AMERICA PAYING ATTENTION

"I’d love for Ben to join me on Skid Row and explain his addiction theory to the methed out psychos skinning dogs alive and sleeping in their own feces," Pratt wrote. "Plenty of suffering out there, and yet…somehow the addiction persists. I wonder what the difference is…"
Fox News Digital has reached out to representatives for Affleck and Pratt for comment.

The 42-year-old "The HIlls" alum, who lost his home in the devastating Palisades Fire in January 2025, announced he was running for Mayor of LA on the one-year anniversary of the disaster. Throughout his campaign, Pratt advocated for active intervention to address the city's overwhelming homelessness crisis, which he described as primarily an addiction issue. He argued that fentanyl and methamphetamine were driving much of the city's visible homelessness.
SPENCER PRATT SEIZES ON HOMELESSNESS REMARKS BY KAREN BASS, BLASTS DEMOCRAT FOR FAILURES
"LA doesn't have a homeless problem. We have a drug problem," Pratt said in March.
The drug addiction crisis in Los Angeles was one of Pratt's signature campaign issues in his run for mayor.  (Etienne Laurent)

Pratt repeatedly argued that people suffering from severe addiction should be placed into involuntary treatment under California's expanded conservatorship law (SB 43), saying many are incapable of seeking help on their own.
In May, he unveiled a five-step plan centered on addiction treatment rather than housing and proposed creating large rehabilitation campuses on federal land outside residential neighborhoods.

His plan also included ending taxpayer-funded distribution of drug paraphernalia, enforcing existing drug laws, partnering with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) to target fentanyl dealers, organized drug trafficking, and international cartels operating in LA and cracking down on what he described as NGOs and organizations that bus addicts into the city from other states to receive services.
As part of his campaign, Pratt highlighted reports of abused dogs on Skid Row, calling the issue another consequence of the city's drug crisis.
Pratt also repeatedly accused his mayoral opponents, Mayor Karen Bass and Councilmember Nithya Raman, of spending billions on homelessness without adequately addressing addiction.

Since conceding the mayoral race in June, Pratt has continued to use his social media platforms to weigh in on political issues, particularly Los Angeles' addiction, homelessness and public safety crises.
Affleck has been open about his decades-long battle with alcoholism.  (Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)
Affleck first sought treatment for alcohol addiction in 2001 and has since spoken candidly about his recovery journey, including subsequent rehab stays in 2017 and 2018.

The "Argo" star has described alcoholism as a lifelong struggle and acknowledged relapses along the way. Affleck has previously said that his three children, Violet, 20, Seraphina, 17, and Samuel, 14, whom he shares with his ex-wife Jennifer Garner, have been a driving force in his commitment to sobriety.
During a 2020 appearance on "ABC News" with Diane Sawyer, Affleck said that his experience growing up with an alcoholic father motivated him to become sober.
The actor has said that his three children have motivated him to stay sober.  (Photo by Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"My dad, he was drunk every day and that was just life," Affleck recalled. "Then as that got worse, that was really, really painful. But I always said, that would never be me. I am never going to do that."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"I wish he had been sober during those formative years, but what he's taught me is, how important it is for me to be sober now during these formative years for my kids," he continued.
"I really don't want my children to pay for my sins," Affleck added "Or to be afraid for me, which is one of the hard parts of being the child of an alcoholic."

title: Tate McRae addresses MAGA speculation after Morgan Wallen collaboration, Jack Hughes controversy
summary: Tate McRae addresses MAGA affiliations tied to her Morgan Wallen collaboration and Jack Hughes' reaction to Trump's hockey call.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Tate McRae addressed MAGA affiliations after being branded a supporter following her country music collaboration.

Tate McRae earned her first No. 1 on the Billboard100 with Morgan Wallen on the country hit "What I Want." (Getty Images)

"I like to say my piece through organizations I support and the environment that I have on tour," she said before the outlet noted that McRae posted a TikTok last year advertising a "Little Miss Possessive" sweatshirt with proceeds going to the Global Fund for Women and The Trevor Project, a suicide prevention nonprofit for LGBTQ+ youth.

"I think it’s pretty obvious what kind of person I am and the things I support."

"There’s always thought about how you want your legacy to go down," she said. title: Scott Eastwood told Shia LaBeouf 'I'm going to whoop your a--' during tense on-set clash
summary: Scott Eastwood detailed the confrontation with Shia LaBeouf, reflected on the actor's intense approach to acting and criticized another unnamed actor who he claims quit a film mid-production.
story: ‘Sarah’s Oil’ star Zachary Levi tells Fox News Digital he was ‘graylisted’ in Hollywood and shares details on his Wyldwood Studios he’s building in Austin, Texas.
Scott Eastwood has a bone to pick with Shia LaBeouf.

During an appearance on Dax Shepard’s "Armchair Expert" podcast, the actor, 40, opened up about a "tense" on-set moment during the filming of the 2014 film, "Fury," in which he nearly got into a physical altercation with the former Disney star.
"There was sort of an incident that happened," Eastwood, 40, said. "I’ve talked about it. Brad Pitt sort of broke up a little, a tense moment."
Eastwood explained that LaBeouf — who played tank gunner Boyd "Bible" Swan in the World War ll movie — was a "very method" actor, who pulled out his tooth and cut himself at one point.

"And I remember thinking, ‘OK, this guy’s crazy. I’m just going to keep clear from this guy.’ I don’t play this game. You go and do that, but there’s plenty of ways to do a performance in a movie and be professional also, right?"
Scott Eastwood said he once threatened to "whoop" Shia LaBeouf's a** while on the set of the 2014 film, "Fury." (Getty Images)

title: Phil Collins' brush with death left his children preparing for the unthinkable
summary: Phil Collins reveals his children were called to say goodbye while he lay unconscious in a Swiss hospital with organs shutting down from alcoholism.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Phil Collins' biggest heartbreak didn't happen onstage.

The music icon revealed the emotional goodbye he shared with his children in 2024 while facing life-threatening health struggles and alcoholism, unsure if he would make it home. Collins' manager called up the singer's five children — Lily, Joely, Simon, Nicolas and Matthew — while he lay unconscious in a Swiss hospital.
"Because there were some decisions to be made about ‘Do we keep Phil on life support?’ kind of thing," he told The Sunday Times.
RANDY TRAVIS' HEALTH CRISIS BEGAN WITH 'CONGESTION' AND ENDED IN A FIVE-MONTH HOSPITAL STAY

Phil Collins recalled fearing he might never see his children again as he battled life-threatening health issues and alcoholism, revealing his family was called to his hospital bedside in 2024 while doctors weighed critical decisions. (Timothy Hiatt/Getty Images)
"My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up," Collins explained. "People were coming to say goodbye."
While Collins has little memory of those harrowing days, his children carried the weight of believing they could be saying their final goodbyes.
"But I don’t remember them coming," he admitted. "I didn’t have no idea this was going on. They were all worried that they wouldn’t see me again. It could all have gone so terribly wrong."
IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

Phil Collins opened up about surviving a life-threatening medical crisis in 2024, sharing that his children gathered to say goodbye while he remained unconscious in a Swiss hospital. (Larry Busacca/Getty Images)
Surviving the ordeal prompted Collins to make a life-changing decision about his drinking.
"I was very lucky to have come out of that," Collins told the publication, adding, "Needless to say, I haven’t had a drink since."

Months later, Collins spent time reconnecting with his kids after surviving the frightening brush with death. Lily "was sitting beside me in tears, saying, ‘I never thought I’d get these moments,'" he recalled.
"We had an incredible time," he added. "I can’t overemphasize how fantastic it was."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
The Genesis legend reflected on his battle with alcoholism and near-death health scare, calling the experience a turning point that led him to give up drinking. (Bob King/Redferns)
His health issues didn't disappear. Collins revealed it's an "ongoing thing" during an appearance on the BBC podcast "Eras" earlier this year.

"I have a 24-hour, live-in nurse to make sure I take my medication as I should do," he explained. "I’ve had challenges with my knee. I had everything that could go wrong with me, did go wrong with me."
Phil Collins at the 2004 Academy Awards with daughters Joely Collins and Lily Collins and ex-wife Orianne Collins. (Bob Riha Jr/WireImage)
Collins has long been candid about the personal battles that accompanied his declining health, including his yearslong struggle with alcoholism.
He built a Hall of Fame career as both the drummer and later lead singer of Genesis before becoming a global solo superstar in the 1980s.
As a solo artist, he sold more than 100 million records worldwide with hits including "In the Air Tonight," "Against All Odds," "Sussudio," "One More Night" and "Another Day in Paradise."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Phil Collins said he was very lucky to survive a life-threatening health ordeal after suffering organ failure, later revealing he has not had a drink since. (Dave J Hogan/Getty Images)
Collins wrote about his struggle with alcoholism in his 2016 autobiography, "Not Dead Yet."

"Night after night I find myself lying on the bed, staring out of a skylight at grey Swiss skies, rueing my life," he wrote, according to People. "I’m all alone, save for my good friends Johnnie Walker and Grey Goose. ‘You’ve got everything,’ I think, ‘but you’ve really got f--k all.'"
Collins didn't shy away from describing how quickly his life unraveled after retirement.

"It took me until the age of 55 to become an alcoholic," he wrote. "I got through the heady Sixties, the trippy Seventies, the imperial Eighties, the busy Nineties. I was retired, content – then I fell. Because suddenly, I had too much time on my hands."
"The huge hole, the void, I had to fill somehow," Collins added. "I filled it with booze. And it nearly killed me."

title: 'The Exorcist' star Linda Blair speaks out after home searched in reported 100-dog kennel investigation
summary: "The Exorcist" star Linda Blair says she and over 100 dogs are fine after Los Angeles County officials executed an inspection warrant on her rescue property in extreme heat.
story: Second Chance Rescue NYC founder Jennifer Brooks tells Fox News Digital passionate advocates like Elaine Hendrix are key as she raises concerns about animal overpopulation at NYC gala event.
Linda Blair is speaking out after authorities searched her Southern California property as part of an active investigation into a reported kennel operation allegedly housing more than 100 dogs.
"The Exorcist" star, 67, said she and the animals in her care are "good" after a "surprise" visit from Los Angeles County officials on Friday.

Officials executed an inspection warrant as part of a joint operation between the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care (DACC) and Control and the Los Angeles County Department of Regional Planning, according to People magazine. Officials told the outlet the operation was intended to evaluate the welfare of the animals and determine whether the property complies with county regulations.

"Checking in, I’m good. The animals are good in lieu of our surprise visit in 105° heat! With as busy as we all are in animal rescue and saving lives from the hot deserts and abandoned animals and shelters, everyone’s emails and social media are overloaded," Blair captioned a video posted to Instagram on July 31.
'EXORCIST' STAR LINDA BLAIR 'UNKNOWINGLY' WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD

"The Exorcist" star Linda Blair speaks out after her California home was visited by authorities as part of an active investigation into a reported kennel operation. (Getty Images; Linda Blair Instagram)

"Turns out we just have some paperwork to do and some diagrams but as everybody knows, I’m looking to move so I can be more educational and help more animals. I’d rather move forward," she continued. "And I always say you know a good old-fashioned letter of contact always works. Be safe safe lives support animal rescue cause we’re all fighting to save lives.
The Oscar-nominated actress added that she has been planning to relocate her rescue operation.
The search was conducted after authorities sought to inspect a property "associated with a kennel operation reported to have more than 100 dogs," per People.
Officials alleged the kennel permits expired in 2023 and claimed multiple attempts to contact the property owner had gone unanswered.

"The warrant allows us to lawfully access the property and verify compliance with County codes," the department said in a statement to People, adding that investigators were assessing "animal care, safety conditions, and overall welfare of the dogs housed on the property."
Blair, who rose to fame in "The Exorcist" in 1973, said the investigation was a mix-up over paperwork. (Getty Images)

"Our priority is the safety and well-being of both the animals on the property and the people who may be working or residing here," the statement continued. "This inspection will help us determine whether conditions meet required standards."
The DACC said the matter remains an active investigation and declined to provide additional details.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"As this is an active and ongoing investigation, DACC is not able to answer specific questions about this case at this time," the department said, adding that it is committed to ensuring kennel operations meet legal requirements and provide humane care.
TMZ, which first reported the search, said Blair was present during the inspection and cooperated with authorities. No dogs were removed from the property, according to the outlet.
Linda Blair "unknowingly" stepped away from acting to launch her Worldheart Foundation in 2003. (Getty Images)
In a video accompanying her Instagram post, Blair reiterated that the visit centered on administrative issues rather than the animals' condition.
"Today we got a really big surprise visit," she said in the video. "And as it turns out, there is nothing but some paperwork and some new diagrams and things."

"Wanted to check in and let you know I am fine. The animals are fine. And we just have some paperwork that has to be dealt with. And that's all this was all about. I don't know why mail isn't used more often to notify somebody. Just saying," she said, while also encouraging supporters to donate to the Linda Blair WorldHeart Foundation — the nonprofit she founded in 2003 to rescue and rehabilitate abused, neglected, and abandoned animals.

title: King Charles makes risky move toward Prince Harry as Prince William 'remains wary': experts
summary: King Charles reportedly plans to offer Prince Harry a room at Buckingham Palace during his September visit, but experts say Prince William is wary.
story: Dan Wakeford, founder of Celebrity Intelligence, discusses Prince Harry's expected UK return, his relationship with King Charles, and why a meeting with Prince William remains unlikely.
Prince Harry's return to the United Kingdom could be King Charles' biggest gamble yet — and Prince William may not like it.

The claim was made by multiple royal experts who spoke to Fox News Digital following reports that the Duke of Sussex is expected to visit the U.K. in September. The Sun reported that the monarch plans to offer his younger son a room at Buckingham Palace in London during his stay.
Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace and Archewell, which oversees the offices of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, for comment.
KING CHARLES SENDS 'DEFIANCE' MESSAGE TO PRINCE WILLIAM WITH BUCKINGHAM PALACE ROOM OFFER TO HARRY: EXPERT

Prince Harry is seen walking behind King Charles during the procession for the lying-in-state of Queen Elizabeth II on Sept. 14, 2022, in London. According to reports, Harry is expected to return to the U.K. in September 2026. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)

"Prince Harry has been invited to stay at Buckingham Palace to coincide with the annual WellChild Awards, which he attends each year," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "This is perceived as an olive branch by King Charles to slowly rebuild their relationship. However, will Prince Harry accept the invitation? There are murmurs that he has accepted it. Time will tell."

"My sources say staff at Buckingham Palace are against Harry staying," Chard said. "They feel immensely betrayed by Harry's explosive claims against the royal family. Also, my sources say there has been no hint of contrition from the Sussexes. People are not going to forget that they hurled the royal family under the bus, creating lasting damage to the crown. Many wonder why King Charles is appeasing Harry."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex departs from The Invictus Games Foundation Conversation: From Policy to Practice at Chatham House on July 7, 2026, in London. Multiple royal experts told Fox News Digital that there's no doubt King Charles' younger son misses his life in the U.K. (Eamonn M. McCormack/Getty Images)

The olive branch came after the Sussexes had a rare reunion with Charles during their visit to the U.K. in July. The private meeting, which took place at Charles' country estate, Highgrove House, marked the first time the king had seen his grandchildren, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, since 2022.
WATCH: PRINCE WILLIAM UNLIKELY TO RECONCILE WITH PRINCE HARRY SOON: EXPERT
Harry's recent visit to the U.K. was marked by problems.

After reports that the prince would visit his home country with his family, the British government declined his request for police protection outside royal residences, prompting him to travel alone on July 6.

Since marrying in 2018 and making their royal exit in 2020, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex have been attempting to carve out their own independent roles outside the monarchy. (Joshua Sammer/Getty Images)

The Sussexes lost their taxpayer-funded security after they stepped back as senior working royals. Harry was later denied the restoration of that security by the Executive Committee for the Protection of Royalty and Public Figures (RAVEC).
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, relocated to California in 2020. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

The couple previously lived at Nottingham Cottage on the grounds of Kensington Palace in London before moving to Frogmore Cottage in Windsor shortly before Archie was born in 2019. After they stepped back as working royals in 2020 and relocated to California, the Sussexes were asked to vacate Frogmore Cottage.
Frogmore Cottage was the home of Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex. (GOR/Getty Images)

People magazine reported that ahead of Harry's trip, his team spent several days exploring ways to make the visit safe through enhanced private security arrangements. Palace sources told the outlet Harry initially declined an invitation to stay at a royal residence before later accepting it.
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, speaks at Scotty's Summer Festival at Maxstoke Castle near Birmingham, central England, on July 11, 2026. (Heathcliff O'Malley/AFP via Getty Images)

Harry's spokesperson told the outlet that an offer for the Duke of Sussex to stay at Buckingham Palace during his London visit was withdrawn after he had formally accepted it. Palace sources, however, disputed that account, saying Harry failed to respond by the deadline and that his later acceptance came only after arrangements could no longer be made.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
A general view of Buckingham Palace in London, England, on July 6, 2026. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)
A source close to the Sussexes told the outlet that, behind the scenes, the drama surrounding the visit was "quite stressful."

"What was billed as a big homecoming ... turned into a nightmare," Russell Myers, author of "William & Catherine," told the outlet. "It was further evidence of the fractiousness of Harry's relationship with the institution."
Prince Harry attends the Time100 Sports Gala at Pier Sixty on July 16, 2026, in New York City. (WWD via Getty Images)

Katie Nicholl, Vanity Fair's royal correspondent, reported that, according to sources, "not even the Prince and Princess of Wales were made aware" that a meeting would take place on July 10 between the Sussexes and the king.

Catherine, Princess of Wales kisses Prince William as she presents the prizes following the DMMI Royal Charity Polo Cup 2026 at The Castle Ground, Guards Polo Club, Flemish Farm, in Windsor, England, on July 10, 2026. At the time, the Sussexes were at Highgrove House with King Charles and Queen Camilla. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

She also reported that Charles, "who has sworn his youngest son and daughter-in-law to secrecy," insisted that nothing about their July 10 meeting be leaked. Only palace aides were permitted to confirm the reunion had taken place after the Sussexes left Highgrove House without being seen.

Royal experts told Fox News Digital that while Charles is open to reconciling with his younger son and reconnecting with his California-based grandchildren, not everyone is welcoming the Sussexes with open arms.

Prince William, Prince of Wales and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex attend the Committal Service for Queen Elizabeth II at St. George's Chapel, Windsor Castle on Sept. 19, 2022, in Windsor, England. (Getty Images)

Prince William is said to remain wary of his estranged brother, many of them shared. According to the experts, the brothers have not spoken since 2022, when their grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, died.

"King Charles, from all indications and all feedback from courtiers, obviously wants to maintain an open dialogue and ongoing relationship with his 'dear boy,'" British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "Prince William, meanwhile, remains wary and won't want Harry at the palace. However, it's better that Harry stays at Buckingham Palace than in Windsor, which is too close to William and his family."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The Sun reported that Prince Harry is expected to visit the U.K. in September and his father, King Charles (center), will offer his son a room at Buckingham Palace in London. (Aaron Chown - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
If Charles hopes to bring Harry back into the royal fold, he'll first need the blessing of the future king, royal expert Richard Fitzwilliams said.

"The attitude of the Waleses, since they are the monarchy's future, is pivotal," Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital. "And with good reason, they don't trust the Sussexes. King Charles' approach could prove incendiary."
British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital there's no feud between Prince William and his father, King Charles III. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Still, Chard believes Charles appears willing to risk fresh royal tensions in pursuit of something he's long wanted: reconciliation with Harry.
King Charles III is seen arriving at Clarence House on Sept. 10, 2025, in London, England. The monarch had a private tea with his son, Prince Harry. (Belinda Jiao/Getty Images)

"Don't get me wrong, reconciliation within the British royal family would be good as it makes the monarchy stronger," Chard said. "However, why invite Harry to Buckingham Palace, the iconic royal residence that's the administrative heart of the monarchy? Harry is no longer a working royal and shouldn't be offered a room at Buckingham Palace."

"I guess the optics of inviting Harry to Buckingham Palace are seen as a goodwill gesture, easing tensions with small steps forward, peace-wise," Chard said. "It also skates over the endless divide within the family."

Britain's Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, looks on as Britain's King Charles III leaves Westminster Abbey after the coronation ceremonies in central London on May 6, 2023. He was sitting a few rows away from his family. (Ben Stansall/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
Chard previously told Fox News Digital that William is known for being stubborn behind palace doors and isn't one to forgive easily.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP

Prince William (pictured here) did not meet with his estranged younger brother, Prince Harry, who spent time with their father King Charles III at Highgrove House, the monarch's private residence, on July 10, 2026. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"William believes the monarchy must be seen to do the right thing, even when it's painful. From what I understand, he felt his father didn't handle that firmly enough. He also believes in protecting it by drawing hard lines. But he's not the king yet."
According to reports, Earl Charles Spencer hosted the Sussexes during their visit to Althorp House. (Jordan Pettitt/PA Images)

During part of their U.K. visit, the Sussexes stayed at Althorp, Princess Diana's ancestral home, where they were hosted by Harry's uncle, Earl Charles Spencer. It was there that Archie and Lilibet learned more about their grandmother, who died when Harry was 12, according to People.
Meghan later shared photos of Harry and their children at the estate on Instagram.
Visitors arrive at Althorp House for the Althorp Literary Festival in Northampton, England. (David Levenson/Getty Images)
Fordwich previously told Fox News Digital that William was likely "livid" over the photos.

"Not only is Prince William likely to be livid regarding the commercialization of Althorp in such a tacky, tasteless media post, but it'll fuel his disgust, so he [would] thwart any major re-entry," she said. "Likewise, Camilla, courtiers, palace aides, security officials and other institutional gatekeepers who are duty-bound to protect the monarchy will all do their utmost to thwart Meghan and Harry's attempts."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Donald Trump's granddaughter Kai Trump reveals her unexpected song of the year pick
summary: Kai Trump revealed Adele's "Rolling in the Deep" as her song of the year in a new video, surprising fans with the classic 2010 hit as her pick.
story: Kai Trump told Fox News Digital that her celebrity crush is no longer "Outer Banks" star Drew Starkey.
Kai Trump surprised fans when she revealed her choice for her "song of the year."

In a video that she shared on her YouTube channel and TikTok, the 19-year-old granddaughter of President Donald Trump admitted that she was caught off guard when she was recently asked to pick a song that "would define your past year."

"And I really did not know. I couldn't think of a song at all. And I'm like, you know what? I just said ‘Rolling in the Deep’ by Adele," Kai said with a laugh. "I don't know, that was like the only song that came up, like came to my head."
President Donald Trump's granddaughter Kai Trump revealed her surprising choice for her song of the year. (Getty Images)
KAI TRUMP REVEALS NEW CELEBRITY CRUSH AFTER DITCHING 'OUTER BANKS' STAR DREW STARKEY

"Rolling in the Deep," which was released in 2010 as the first single off Adele's second studio album "21," is widely considered the singer's breakthrough hit. "Rolling in the Deep" reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart where it spent seven weeks at the top.
The song, which also topped the charts in more than a dozen countries, won three Grammy Awards in 2012 including record of the year, song of the year and best short form music video.
"Rolling in the Deep" is credited with helping launch Adele into global superstardom and is still regarded as one of her signature songs alongside "Someone Like You" and "Hello."
The 19-year-old named Adele's 2010 mega-hit "Rolling in the Deep" as the song that "defined" her year. (Denise Truscello/Getty Images for AD)

Kai has previously named "Rolling in the Deep" as one of her favorite songs. During a video that she shared on her YouTube channel in March, Kai participated in an "Ask Me Anything" Q&A session with her fans, in which she was asked about her favorite song. Along with "Rolling in the Deep, Kai also said her top picks include "November Rain" by Guns N' Roses and "House of Balloons" by the Weeknd.
"Or ‘After Party’ by the Weeknd,: she added. "Also ‘Wicked Games’ by the Weeknd. I love The Weeknd."
Kai has previously said that she "loves' The Weeknd.  (Paras Griffin)

Kai regularly gives fans a glimpse into her personal favorites including food, hobbies and celebrities during social media Q&As and interviews. During an interview with Fox News Digital, Kai revealed that she had a new celebrity crush after previously naming "Outer Banks" star Drew Starkey in 2024.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"I think Theo James now, yeah, Theo James, I would say, so it's changed," Kai began. "I mean, like, I still like him [Starkey], but it's just changed a little."
When asked why James has taken her No. 1 spot, the 19-year-old gushed over his looks.
"He's very attractive," Kai said of James, 41.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Kai recently revealed Theo James as her new celebrity crush.  (Photo by River Callaway/Variety via Getty Images)
Two years ago, Kai took to her YouTube channel to answer questions that her fans submitted on X. In a clip titled "Get to know me better…Q&A," one social media user asked, "Celebrity crush?"

Before responding, Kai asked for her phone, noting she "had to look up" her celebrity crush. Upon glancing at the screen, she said, "Oh my God, I know. Why do I need my phone? His name is Drew Starkey. Do you guys know him — ‘Outer Banks?’"
"I'm gonna blush right now!" Kai added as her cheeks turned red, and she fanned herself with her hand.
Kai, who frequently golfs with Trump, will compete on the University of Miami's women's golf team in the fall.  (Michele Eve Sandberg/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)
Kai told Fox News Digital that having her grandfather in office has made her dating life "tricky."

"It's not easy, to be honest with you, but, you know, you gotta live life," she said. "You gotta just keep on doing normal stuff, you know? At the end of the day, I was in high school, lived a normal high school life, and now I'm going to college. So, just kinda live as normal of a life as possible."

The oldest child of Donald Trump Jr. and Vanessa Trump is set to begin her freshman year at the University of Miami this fall. Kai, who frequently plays golf with her grandfather, will compete on the Hurricanes women's golf team during the 2026-27 season.

title: Rock star kicked off tour amid allegations of inappropriate messages with a minor
summary: Simon O'Connor claims a tasteless meme sent to a minor was a case of mistaken identity after a Reddit post surfaced with screenshot evidence.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Modest Mouse dropped guitarist Simon O'Connor from upcoming tour dates amid accusations that the musician sent inappropriate messages to a minor.
The band announced O'Connor – who joined the band in 2021 – was no longer part of the tour in a post shared on social media last week.
"Simon O'Connor will not be joining us on the upcoming tour," the band wrote. "The good news is that Seth Jabour of Les Savy Fav will be jumping in to play guitar."
They added, "We look forward to being out there with you all."
JARED LETO RESPONDS TO SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS MADE BY MULTIPLE WOMEN IN EXPLOSIVE DOCUMENTARY
Simon O'Connor was kicked off the Modest Mouse tour amid allegations that he sent inappropriate messages to a minor. (Jim Bennett)
Modest Mouse representatives did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

In a post shared on Reddit last month, a 16-year-old female fan uploaded screenshots and claimed O'Connor sent her an "erotic image," followed by a slew of direct messages after she liked some of the musician's Instagram stories.
JASON ALEXANDER APOLOGIZES AFTER COURTNEY STODDEN SAYS 2012 COMEDY SKETCH OBJECTIFIED HER AS A MINOR

The accuser allegedly indicated her age on her handle at the time, and commented on the thread, "For context the story I had that he viewed was my 17th birthday countdown and it said that very clearly."

She claimed that O'Connor quickly deleted the message, and proceeded to engage in a thread where he admitted his phone wasn't "hacked" and that he "just had a party night and looking at everything with one eye ya know."

The accuser wrote, "oh boy get a good night of sleep," before O'Connor appeared to respond back, "But you did blindside me with a gaggle of likes and then very little intro besides bikini pics so we are both to blame."
FORMER DISNEY TEEN STAR EXPOSES CHILLING WARNING SIGNS OF PREDATORY BEHAVIOR IN HOLLYWOOD
A following screenshot appeared to show the message deleted, with O'Connor writing, "I did it again."
Modest Mouse first formed in 1993 with Isaac Brock as lead singer, late drummer Jeremiah Green and bassist Eric Judy. (Jim Bennett)
O'Connor addressed the incident the following day, and stated: "I unequivocally oppose any sexual behavior towards minors, as a human and a parent it disgusts me."

"Throughout my adult life, there has been a person who has popped up from time to time with the intention of, for lack of a better term, messing with me," he wrote. "This person creates multiple social media accounts and deletes them… but always posts similar photos that I often recognize from previous accounts.
"After a long night, I picked my phone up to discover that a similar profile had been interacting ('likes' to be specific) with some of my instagram posts and stories."

O'Connor "assumed" he was dealing with the same person as before, and "with poor judgement, I decided to reach out with a tasteless meme, a sticker that read 'Simon calls your bluff,' and an attempt to indicate that I recognized the 'barrage of likes' and similar photo content from the previous profiles…. Almost a 'gotcha.'"
Simon O'Connor played with the indie band for five years. (Daniel Knighton)
"After a few minutes, I realized that I had made a mistake and this was not the person who I had dealt with before. I unsent the messages and immediately ceased communication," he wrote.

"I'm genuinely sorry to the person who received those messages. They didn't deserve to be put in that position, and I'm sorry for the stress and attention this has brought them."

He added, "I know some people will choose not to believe me, and I understand that. I can't change what's happened. All I can do is tell the truth, take responsibility for my mistake, and apologize."
O'Connor previously toured with MGMT, and appears on Modest Mouse's latest album, "An Eraser and a Maze."

title: Landman' star Ali Larter shows off her fit physique in barely-there bikinis during yacht vacation in Italy
summary: Ali Larter, 50, shared stunning bikini photos from her Italian superyacht vacation, showcasing the fitness routine that keeps her camera-ready.
story: Ali Larter told Fox News Digital that her summers look a lot different 6 years after ditching LA for Idaho.
Ali Larter flaunted her fit physique in several skimpy bikinis while soaking up the sun during a vacation in Italy.
On Saturday, the 50-year-old actress shared a carousel of photos featuring moments from her getaway on a superyacht in the Italian Rivera.
In one snap, the "Landman" star rocked a nude-toned metallic bikini as she sunbathed on a red and white lounge chair while out at sea.
'LANDMAN' STAR ALI LARTER ESCAPED TO IDAHO AFTER HOLLYWOOD'S 'MANY' SOCIAL DEMANDS

Larter's two-piece featured a ruched bandeau top with a circle keyhole cutout and bottoms that had gold chain detailing on the sides. She accessorized with black oval sunglasses and several gold rings.
Ali Larter attends Elle World at the Hall des Lumières on June 20, 2026, in New York City. (GC Images)
The "Varsity Blues" actress draped one arm over the cushion behind her head as she beamed at the camera.

In a selfie, Larter donned a black bandeau bikini top accented with gold hardware and black ruffled shorts while cozying up to her husband Hayes MacArthur as they posed at the side of the yacht against a backdrop of the rocky coastline and ocean.

Larter wore a lingerie-style white lace halter top bikini with nude lining in another photo that she shared. She wore the two-piece under a sheer aquamarine blue cover-up that was embellished with white and turquoise stones that lined Larter's neckline and chest.
The actress rocked a metallic nude bikini with gold chains.  (Ali Larter Instagram )
In the image, Larter posed for the camera as she descended wooden steps on the yacht under a blue sky dotted with white clouds.

The "Final Destination" star also showed off more of her summer style, sporting a plunging light blue and white printed minidress while standing in front of a bar and flashing a bright smile. She was also pictured in a brightly-colored flowing cover-up as she strolled on the deck of the yacht.

Larter, who is known for her dedication to fitness, was seen in a black Alo sports bra with matching leggings during a workout session in a gym on the yacht.

In her carousel, Larter included other photos featuring a plate of pasta with a glass of wine, a sunset and a selfie in which she was seen wearing a red top with a diamond necklace and a headset. Later concluded her slideshow with a loved-up snap of herself with MacArthur that was taken on the yacht at night.
"🇮🇹 Adoro l’Italia 🇮🇹," she wrote in the caption of her post.
Larter wore a black bikini while cozying up with her husband.  (Ali Larter Instagram )
While Larter has occasionally shared swimsuit photos on her Instagram page, the actress previously admitted her bikini scenes in "Landman" are the most challenging for her to film.
SHAKIRA SOAKS UP THE MIAMI SUN AS BIKINI-CLAD NINA DOBREV, KIM KARDASHIAN SHOWCASE SUMMER GETAWAYS

During a January interview with People magazine, the 49-year-old actress, who plays Angela Norris in the hit Paramount+ series, described shooting scenes in which her character wears a bikini as "tough, in a weird way."
"I don't think there's an actress alive that's like, 'Woo! Got a bikini scene!' " Larter said. "Nobody wants to do it.
"Those are the hardest for me," she continued. "I don't enjoy them. It's just part of the story that I'm telling, and I'm an actress, so I get on board. But those are definitely my least favorite."
Larter donned a white lace bikini under a sheer aqua blue cover-up.  (Ali Larter Instagram )
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Angela is the confident and glamorous ex-wife of Billy Bob Thornton's Tommy Norris. The "Varsity Blues" star noted that her character is "so physical and loves the spray tans, and the blonde."
Larter explained that portraying Angela, who is often clad in revealing clothing, requires effort and discipline to ensure that she is "staying in shape for this role and all that comes with it."
While speaking with People in November, Larter shared how she adheres to a strict diet and fitness routine while filming the show.
Larter sported atheisure as she showed off her workout on the yacht.  (Ali Larter Instagram )
HILARIA BALDWIN FLAUNTS FIT FIGURE IN BIKINI AS FANS MARVEL AT MOM OF 7

"I'll tell you what. I work really hard, OK? I'm not pretending that I don't," she said. "I'm up at 4:30 [a.m.] on Mondays. I go for a run. It's only 30 minutes. I try to eat very clean, but I eat. I'm one of those protein mommies. I eat so much protein all day long. It works for me."
She explained that, in addition to running, she also does "a lot of strength training."

"In the end, anytime you have to put on a bathing suit and walk in front of anybody, it's really difficult," she said. "When I look around, the sexiest women I know are the women that own it. So, part of getting there with Angela is owning it."
"But no matter what, it's like, I've got to spend all this time fighting off my own insecurities, my own anxiety, to be able to put on that bikini and walk into these scenes," she admitted.
Larter told People that "there is no space in my mind for insecurity" when playing Angela.
Michelle Randolph as Ainsley Norris and Ali Larter as Angela Norris in season one of "Landman." (Emerson Miller/Paramount+.)

title: Amy Schumer earns praise for sharing unfiltered bikini photos amid her weight-loss journey
summary: Amy Schumer shared new bikini photos showing her weight loss results after crediting Mounjaro and hormone therapy for perimenopause symptoms.
story: The supermodel tells Fox News Digital at The Paley Center Gala in New York the healthy habits she prioritizes in summer.
Amy Schumer is soaking up what's left of summer — and showing off the results of her recent weight loss.

The 45-year-old comedian shared a series of bikini photos on Instagram over the weekend, posing confidently in a colorful two-piece while enjoying time by the water. Schumer smiled for the camera as she relaxed waterside, offering fans a glimpse at her recent getaway.
"I never knew there would be days like this," she captioned the post. "No filter as per ushe."
HILARIA BALDWIN FLAUNTS FIT FIGURE IN BIKINI AS FANS MARVEL AT MOM OF 7
Amy Schumer showed off her weight loss in a series of bikini photos over the weekend. (Getty Images; Amy Schumer Instagram)
Schumer quickly earned praise from friends and fans.
"So beautiful, Amy. Happy and thriving," actress Kate Walsh commented.
"Gorgeous," another wrote.
The actress has been open with fans about her evolving relationship with her health and body over the past two years, documenting both the highs and lows of her weight-loss journey.
APP USERS CLICK HERE TO VIEW POST

In October, Schumer took to social media to share a photo of her dramatic transformation. Schumer, who was wearing a tiny black dress and heels, was accompanied by two friends as the group enjoyed the Paul McCartney concert in Las Vegas.
Friends and fans were quick to share their thoughts, praising the actress for her progress.
'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE ISSUES WARNING ABOUT WEIGHT LOSS DRUG CRAZE
"Okay Amyyyyyy🔥" comedian Anjelah Johnson commented.
"Those legs ❤️❤️❤️" Isla Fisher wrote.
Amy Schumer shares photos from her tropical getaway. (Amy Schumer Instagram)
In March 2025, Schumer praised the effects of Mounjaro (also known as tirzepatide) in a video clip shared on Instagram with her nearly 13 million followers.

"I wanted to share and keep it 100 with you, that years ago – and yes, this is completely unsafe to be driving and making a video – years ago, three years ago, I tried Wegovy and I was like puking," Schumer said in the clip captured while she was behind the wheel.

"I couldn't handle it. I don't know if they've changed the formula or whatever… but anyway, I went on this telehealth meeting with MidiHealth, and it was cheap. I wanted to try it myself, cause I wanted to recommend it to my friends who are like nurses and teachers."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
In addition to the injectable medication, which is primarily used to treat type 2 diabetes, the "Trainwreck" star detailed a new routine which includes hormones.
"They put me on estrogen and progesterone because I realized I was in perimenopause and my symptoms of being in perimenopause have disappeared," Schumer said.
It took trial and error to find what worked for her.
Amy Schumer poses on a carpeted staircase while wearing a light cream dress, shown in both a full-body shot and a close-up portrait. (Amy Schumer/Instagram)
During an appearance on "The Howard Stern Show" last year, the comedian opened up about her scary experience trying medication for weight-loss purposes.

"I have this gene – GDF15 – which makes you extremely prone to nausea, which is why I was so sick during my pregnancy. So, I tried Ozempic almost three years ago and I was like bedridden, I was vomiting, and then you have no energy but other people take it, and they're all good," she explained.

"I lost 30 pounds so quick," said Schumer, who is mom to 4-year-old son Gene, whom she shares with ex-husband, Chris Fischer. "I looked great, and I couldn't lift my head off the pillow, so what's the point?"

Schumer has long been outspoken about body image and the pressure women face in Hollywood. Rather than shying away from criticism, Schumer has often used humor to address comments about her appearance while encouraging others to focus on their health instead of unrealistic beauty standards.
Amy Schumer admitted to suffering a medical setback during an appearance in New York with Amanda Hirsch. (Theo Wargo)

In February 2024, Schumer revealed she had been diagnosed with Cushing syndrome after fans questioned the swelling in her face. She later said she viewed the diagnosis as a blessing because it led doctors to uncover the underlying cause.

Over the years, Schumer has also been candid about living with endometriosis and undergoing a hysterectomy in 2021, frequently sharing updates about her health to help normalize conversations around women's medical issues.

title: Stephen Baldwin on choosing born-again Christianity over Hollywood after a life-changing encounter with God
summary: Stephen Baldwin reveals how a Brazilian housekeeper's prophecy and a skateboarding ministry led him to leave Hollywood after finding mega success.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Stephen Baldwin believes he could have been one of Hollywood's biggest stars, but he doesn't regret leaving the business for something far more important: his faith.

In a new interview, Baldwin, 60, reflected on the career-defining success that followed his role in the Oscar-winning 1995 crime thriller, "The Usual Suspects," and opened up about why he never felt drawn to chase stardom.

"I probably could have pointed myself in the direction of becoming a big star," Baldwin told People. "But that wasn't me. I didn't want to be Tom Cruise, and have to make $100 million at the box office. I'd rather be a schmuck from Massapequa."
HEATHER LOCKLEAR SAYS SHE LIVES 'FAR AWAY' FROM HOLLYWOOD AND STAYS OUT OF THE SOCIAL SCENE
Stephen Baldwin left Hollywood after finding faith. (Getty Images)
Baldwin said his priorities shifted dramatically after embracing born-again Christianity in 2001.

According to the actor, his faith journey began after he and his wife, Kennya, hired a Brazilian housekeeper who claimed she had been sent by God because the couple would one day become Christians and start a ministry.

"My wife tells me, ‘I just spoke to Augusta, and she said the real reason she’s here is because God spoke to her, and she said in the future you and I will become born-again Christians and have our own ministry,’" Baldwin told the outlet.
JD VANCE REVEALS WHAT DREW HIM BACK TO GOD AFTER SEEING CHRISTIANS HAD LIFE ‘FIGURED OUT’

At first, Baldwin admitted he was skeptical. However, after attending a handful of evangelical events with his sister — who had already become a born-again Christian — and witnessing a Christian skateboarding ministry that blended extreme sports with worship, he said everything shifted.
Brothers Alec Baldwin and Stephen Baldwin have always supported each other throughout the years. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

"Down on the beach, they had built a skate park on the sand with plywood. And these funky, super committed, cool, tattooed, pierced skateboarders were there and they’d skate, stop, pick up a microphone and start preaching evangelistically, and like 5,000 kids would be around watching because of their interest in the skateboarders," he recalled. "I felt a calling."
Baldwin eventually created a skate video with a Christian message, titled "Livin' It."
FORMER SUPERMODEL SAYS CELEBRITIES NEED TO 'WAKE UP' AND RECOGNIZE CHRISTIAN FANS

"In the first six months we’d distributed 10,000 copies. Then one of the bigger churches called and asked what it would cost to bring the skaters from the video to their church for a live event. So that’s when I left Hollywood," he said. "I went to 125 churches over four years," he said. "Jesus and the Holy Spirit fascinated me."
Baldwin admitted that Hollywood hasn't always been super accepting of his religious and political outspokenness.
"I think they thought I act a little too weird," said Baldwin, who supported President Donald Trump in 2016 and 2024.

"I get a lot of DMs from people who tell me how my work has touched them and that’s all that matters. I’m happy to be where I’m now at 60. I’m so blessed. And I absolutely believe that the best is yet to come."
These days, Stephen Baldwin is enjoying being a grandfather and focusing on faith-filled projects.

Today, Baldwin says he's focused on producing faith-based films for younger audiences while hosting his podcast, "One Bad Movie," where actors discuss the worst film or filming experience of their careers.

The actor also said becoming a grandfather has only strengthened his perspective on life.
"I've done 100 movies, I've made more money than I could have wildly imagined, and I'm married to the hottest chick I've ever seen in my life," Baldwin said. "Jesus is my rock. My wife is my anchor."

title: Tick-borne 'rabbit fever' spreads with cases reported near major metro area
summary: Three probable tularemia cases on Long Island have officials warning residents about the tick-borne illness after a 9-year-old developed severe symptoms.
story: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel discusses the surge in Powassan tick-borne virus cases, prevention methods and treatments. The rare virus, often carried by deer and mice, has seen a record number of reported cases this year.
Health officials on Long Island are warning residents about a rare but potentially serious tick-borne illness.
Three probable cases of tularemia — also known as "rabbit fever" — have been confirmed by the Suffolk County Department of Health Services (SCDHS).

"SCDHS currently has three probable cases of tularemia this year," the agency said in a statement provided to local outlets. "Confirmation of a tularemia diagnosis requires a combination of laboratory testing and fulfillment of specific clinical or epidemiologic criteria. The laboratory testing to confirm a tularemia diagnosis may take several weeks."
NO CURE, NO VACCINE: EXPERTS WARN OF RARE BOURBON VIRUS AFTER FIRST NY CASE

One case involved a 9-year-old patient who was bitten by a tick while playing outside, according to NBC4 New York. After the tick was removed, he later developed high fever, severe head and neck pain, swollen lymph nodes/glands, body aches and extreme fatigue.
After multiple doctor visits and nearly a month of illness, an infectious disease specialist diagnosed the boy with tularemia.
Health officials on Long Island are warning residents about a rare but potentially serious tick-borne illness. (iStock)

Although the family's yard is home to wild rabbits, the patient's mother said he never handled the animals. Doctors believe infected ticks likely fed on the rabbits before biting the boy, transmitting the bacteria, according to reports.
What to know about rabbit fever
Caused by the bacteria Francisella tularensis, the disease commonly infects rabbits, hares and rodents. However, it is zoonotic, which means it can spread from animals to humans.

The bacteria is a "tier-1 select agent," a classification given to agents and toxins that "present the greatest risk of deliberate misuse with significant potential for mass casualties or devastating effects to the economy, critical infrastructure or public confidence, and pose a severe threat to public health and safety," per the CDC.
TICK BITE ER VISITS HIT HIGHEST SEASONAL LEVEL IN YEARS AS DOCTORS WARN OF DISEASE SURGE

Although tularemia remains rare, with 196 U.S. cases reported in 2023, the disease has become more common in recent years. CDC surveillance found 2,462 cases between 2011 and 2022 — a 56% increase in incidence compared with the previous decade (2001–2010).

Daniel Ruderfer, M.D., chief of the Division of Pediatric Infectious Diseases at Hackensack Meridian K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital in New Jersey, believes that the increase in cases is mostly due to improved microbiology detection methods.
Caused by the bacteria Francisella tularensis, the disease commonly infects rabbits, hares and rodents. However, it is zoonotic, which means it can spread from animals to humans. (iStock)
"The traditional method of confirming cases has historically been via growth in culture and antibody testing," he previously told Fox News Digital.
"However, newer detection methods, such as PCR testing, are likely a major contributor to the increase in reported cases."

Humans can contract the disease through bites from deer flies or ticks, contact with infected animals, or exposure to contaminated water or aerosols, the same source stated.

Symptoms of tularemia can vary depending on the type of disease. General symptoms include chills, headache, malaise, fatigue, anorexia, myalgia, chest discomfort, cough, severe sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, according to Ruderfer.
Humans can contract the disease through bites from deer flies or ticks, contact with infected animals, or exposure to contaminated water or aerosols. (iStock)
"Depending on the location of the infected bit or scratch, people can develop localized lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes) and a cutaneous ulcer at the infection site," he said.
"Other manifestations include conjunctivitis, pneumonia and potentially even bloodstream infections."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
The death rate from the disease is typically low, less than 2%, but the CDC noted that it can be as high as 24% in rare, severe cases.
Tularemia can be treated with antibiotics, but no vaccine is currently available.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"The infection is absolutely dangerous and potentially life-threatening if not treated with appropriate antibiotics," said Ruderfer.
Those most at risk include children between 5 and 9 years of age, older men, American Indian and Alaskan Native people, and those living in central U.S. states, according to the report.
"The infection is absolutely dangerous and potentially life-threatening if not treated with appropriate antibiotics."
The general population is not at an "obvious" risk for infection unless they come into physical contact with an infected rabbit, tick or deer fly, the expert noted.

Those who hunt or interact routinely with rabbits should see a doctor if they develop any concerning symptoms, he advised.

"Many factors might contribute to the higher risk for tularemia in this population, including the concentration of Native American reservations in central states and sociocultural or occupational activities that might increase contact with infected wildlife or arthropods," the CDC wrote.
