title: Don't let fake election websites fool you before 2026 midterms
summary: Over 62,000 election-named domains were tracked since September 2025, with some active storefronts copying campaign branding to collect donations.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

You spot a campaign shirt online that makes you laugh. The site carries the candidate's name. It also has polished product photos and a familiar checkout page. So, you assume the store supports the campaign.
A fake election website can copy enough campaign cues to make that assumption feel reasonable. Your money and personal information could then reach an operator with no verified campaign connection.

New research provided to CyberGuy by WhoisXML API, an internet intelligence company that analyzes domain, IP and DNS data, tracked 62,081 election-named domains created since September 2025. Researchers identified 13,645 addresses that read like campaign sites based on their names.

The research classifies only a portion of the domains as campaign-style addresses. Legitimate campaigns, supporters, merchants and domain investors may control many of them. However, researchers also found live storefronts that used candidates' names while selling merchandise and accepting donation-style payments. That smaller group creates the clearest risk for you.
FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK
Voters should verify campaign websites, donation links and committee disclaimers before entering personal or payment information. (Getty Images)
CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?," has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.
Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
Why fake election websites surge before the midterms

National elections create a rush for online real estate. Campaign teams want memorable web addresses before someone else claims them. Supporters may launch fan pages, while merchants see an opportunity to sell political products. Impersonators can follow the same naming formula.

According to WhoisXML API, nearly 46% of the curated campaign-style set used structures such as "[name]for[office]" or "for[state]." Domains referencing congressional races appeared most often. Senate-themed names came next. State names also appeared across about one-third of the curated set. Texas led with 537 registrations. Florida, Georgia, Ohio and Colorado followed.

Those names feel familiar because real campaigns use the same structure. As a result, a questionable domain can look credible before you open the page. Across the domains studied, researchers said 90% hid the registrant's identity. In addition, 88% carried a one-year registration term. Privacy protection and short registration terms can have legitimate uses. Still, those details deserve more attention when a new site also copies campaign branding or asks for money.
How fake election websites copy real campaign stores

A small change in a domain can hide in plain sight. WhoisXML API highlighted massiemoneybomb[.]us, which closely resembled the established massiemoneybomb[.]com fundraising address. The main difference appeared after the final dot.

That change may look obvious on a large computer screen. However, it becomes easier to miss on a phone, especially when a text or social media post opens the page directly. Researchers also examined kenpaxton[.]us. They said the domain was 58 days old when captured, while kenpaxton[.]com dated back to 2008.

The newer site reportedly sold supportive campaign products alongside merchandise criticizing the same candidate. That unusual mix offers a clue that the store may lack an official connection. Yet many shoppers will focus on the product photos or the price. A polished checkout can make the entire operation feel established. Alexandre François, the WhoisXML API domain scam researcher behind the study, told CyberGuy that AI can help operators build convincing websites quickly and at scale. That makes it even harder to judge a campaign page by its appearance alone.
How fake election donation pages collect personal data

Political merchandise may cost you more than the price on the screen. According to the research, some storefronts allowed visitors to add donation-style payments of up to $1,000 to a shopping cart. The sites then processed the payment through their own checkout flows.

One store reportedly continued accepting a donation-style payment after the candidate's official ActBlue page stopped taking contributions. The checkout requested a full name, street address, email address and phone number. It also collected payment card details.

A familiar payment processor can make that form feel safe. However, its presence only shows how the payment moves through the checkout. It cannot confirm that the candidate authorized the store or that the campaign receives the money.

François said the study found no direct evidence that donors lost money or had their data misused. "Only the payment platforms could see whether a donor lost money or had data misused, and their data was not part of this study," he told CyberGuy. The findings support caution rather than a claim that every highlighted site committed fraud.
What domain records reveal about fake election websites

Domain registration records can expose useful clues before or after a website launches. Researchers can review the creation date, registrar, paid registration period and privacy status. Sometimes, the records also identify the owner or registrant country. However, each clue has limits.

Many legitimate website owners use privacy services to keep home addresses and contact details out of public databases. Campaigns may also register several defensive domains so impersonators cannot claim them first. A one-year registration term also appears across ordinary websites. Price and convenience often drive that choice.
The risk grows when several details point in the same direction. A nearly copied domain may lead to a new storefront with an unofficial donation flow. A mismatched disclaimer adds another concern.

For federal political committees, public websites generally need a disclaimer that identifies who paid for the communication. The wording may also state whether a candidate authorized it. The FEC explains that disclaimer requirements cover political committee websites and online fundraising communications. A disclaimer cannot guarantee honesty. Still, a missing or mismatched statement gives you a strong reason to leave the page and verify the site elsewhere.

Campaigns also face limits when trying to secure every possible variation of a candidate's name. François said they should consistently promote one official domain and one donation link. He added that "the realistic option is monitoring" because registering every possible look-alike domain would be impractical. Monitoring new registrations can help campaigns find look-alike sites during their first days online. Campaigns can then report suspicious pages to the registrar, hosting company or payment provider.
SAME-NAME CANDIDATE DISQUALIFIED FROM KEY SENATE RACE OVER ALLEGED DEM SCHEME TO CONFUSE VOTERS
Fake election websites, like the one pictured, can copy campaign branding, storefront designs and donation pages to collect money and personal information. (WhoisXML API)
Ways to stay safe from fake election websites
Before you buy campaign merchandise or make a political contribution online, use these checks to confirm that the site connects to the candidate or committee you intend to support.

Avoid starting with a link from an unexpected text, email, online ad or social media comment. Instead, search for the candidate independently. Then compare the result with links from the candidate's verified social media account or established public profile. "No single sign is enough, so it's best to check a few together and to reach the page from the campaign's own channel," François told CyberGuy.

You can also use a personal data removal service to reduce the personal information available through data brokers and people-search sites. This may limit the details scammers can use to make unexpected messages, targeted ads or social media comments feel more convincing. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

For federal races, use the FEC's campaign finance database at fec.gov/data/ to look up candidates and registered committees. The database shows federal candidate and committee filings. For state or local races, check the appropriate state or local election authority. Many campaigns process contributions through ActBlue or WinRed. In those cases, the payment address should show secure.actblue.com or secure.winred.com. Some campaigns use other processors, so an unfamiliar payment provider alone does not prove the page is deceptive.
Tap or click the address bar before entering payment information. Check the spelling and domain ending. Then look for added words or letters that imitate the campaign's real address.

A scammer may replace ".com" with ".us." Another operator may add words such as "official," "store," "donate," or "support" to make the address feel authentic. François said the difference may also involve one word, a hyphen or an ending such as ".vote" or ".store."

Scroll to the bottom of the site and review the area around the donation form. A federal political committee website should identify who paid for the communication. Depending on the committee, the disclaimer may also explain whether the candidate authorized it.

Compare that committee name with the FEC database. Leave the page when the names conflict or the disclosure looks vague. Keep in mind that a deceptive page can copy a real committee's name. Treat the disclosure as one clue rather than proof that the page belongs to the campaign.
Open the candidate's established website in a separate tab. Look for a direct link to the merchandise store or donation page. If the official site sends you somewhere else, use the link it provides.

Also review the store's contact details and return policy. Be cautious if it sells products supporting a candidate alongside merchandise attacking that candidate. That unusual mix may signal the store has no official campaign connection. A page that keeps collecting contributions after a candidate withdraws also deserves closer scrutiny. The same applies when a store continues selling campaign merchandise after the official donation page closes.
The padlock in your browser means the site uses an encrypted connection. It offers no proof about the person or business behind the page.

CISA warns that phishing attacks may use malicious websites that impersonate trusted organizations to collect personal information. A professional design and secure connection still require you to verify the operator.
Pressure can push you past obvious warning signs. Be cautious when a site claims a donation match will disappear within minutes. A countdown clock that keeps resetting should also raise concern.
The FTC's broader donation-safety guidance recommends researching an organization and resisting pressure to give immediately.
WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME
Researchers found campaign-style websites selling political merchandise and accepting donation-style payments under candidates’ names. (yasindmrblk/Getty Images)

A credit card generally offers stronger dispute protections than a debit card. It also keeps the payment away from funds in your checking account. The FTC says legal protections for credit cards exceed those for debit cards in billing disputes.

Save your receipt and take screenshots of the product page and checkout. Make sure the full domain appears in at least one image. After you pay, check your statement to confirm the amount and make sure the site did not enroll you in recurring contributions.

A fake campaign website may try to push a malicious download or send you to another harmful page. Strong antivirus software can help detect suspicious files and block some dangerous websites. However, you still need to verify the campaign connection before you pay. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

If a store asks you to create an account, use a unique password. A password manager can generate and save a strong password for you, so you do not have to remember it. Reusing a password could put your other accounts at risk if the login information gets exposed. Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) when the site offers it.
What to do after paying through a fake election website

Contact your card issuer or bank as soon as you suspect a problem.Explain what happened and ask whether it can reverse the transaction. The FTC advises consumers who paid a suspected scammer by credit or debit card to contact the issuer and request a reversal.Next, report suspected fraud through the FTC's ReportFraud system. If the site may have violated federal campaign finance law, you can also review the FEC complaint process.The FEC accepts complaints about possible violations involving federal election financing. Its authority covers elections for the U.S. House, Senate and president.Watch your statements for unfamiliar charges. Also change any password that you reused on the store.If the website collected information that later appears in identity fraud, IdentityTheft.gov can create a recovery plan and guide you through the next steps.
Contact your card issuer or bank as soon as you suspect a problem.
Explain what happened and ask whether it can reverse the transaction. The FTC advises consumers who paid a suspected scammer by credit or debit card to contact the issuer and request a reversal.
Next, report suspected fraud through the FTC's ReportFraud system. If the site may have violated federal campaign finance law, you can also review the FEC complaint process.
The FEC accepts complaints about possible violations involving federal election financing. Its authority covers elections for the U.S. House, Senate and president.
Watch your statements for unfamiliar charges. Also change any password that you reused on the store.
If the website collected information that later appears in identity fraud, IdentityTheft.gov can create a recovery plan and guide you through the next steps.
Kurt's key takeaways on fake election websites

Election season gives questionable websites a powerful disguise. A candidate's name can create trust before you verify who operates the page. The scale of this research should make every online donor slow down. Researchers found more than 62,000 election-named domains, though many may serve legitimate purposes. The clearest concern comes from active storefronts that copy campaign-style branding and collect money outside a verified campaign path. Take an extra minute before buying a shirt or making a contribution. Find the official campaign site through a trusted source. Then confirm the web address and committee disclosure before you enter personal or payment information.

title: Luigi Mangione's livestream stunt aims to get influencers to 'pressure' jurors: former prosecutor
summary: A former federal prosecutor says Luigi Mangione's push to livestream his murder trial is designed to pressure jurors and fuel jury nullification.
story: Former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani says Mangione's demand to livestream his murder trial is a 'stunt' aimed at letting influencers sway jurors — and could fuel a push for jury nullification or even an acquittal.
Luigi Mangione's push to livestream his murder trial isn't about transparency, it's a stunt designed to pressure jurors, a former federal prosecutor is arguing.
Lawyers for the accused UnitedHealthcare CEO assassin argued in a Friday filing that the media access rules for his state trial are unconstitutional, and said the proceedings should be livestreamed.

Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Mangione's attorney, said that her team wasn't consulted on media access for the upcoming September trial, and only became aware of a document titled "Media Access: PSNY v. Mangione" from an independent journalist on X.
MANGIONE LAWYERS SAY MEDIA LIMITS AT MURDER TRIAL ARE UNCONSTITUTIONAL, FEAR COURT WILL 'HAND-PICK' PRESS

UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, left, pictured in a corporate headshot. He was killed on Dec. 4, 2024, outside a Manhattan hotel while on his way to a shareholder conference. The suspect, Luigi Mangione, is pictured in court on the right. (Businesswire, Steven Hirsch for New York Post via Pool)

Former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani, president of West Coast Trial Lawyers, told Fox News Digital he believes Mangione's attorneys want all trial proceedings to be livestreamed to pressure jurors, noting it's unusual for defendants to want more publicity.

"The conventional wisdom is that the defense usually doesn't want high-profile cases broadcast. It can put implicit pressure on jurors to return a guilty verdict," Rahmani said. "Mangione is probably the most popular accused murderer that I've ever covered in the past 25 years. Has a fan base. There's upwards of 10 to 20 percent of the people who have been surveyed who believe that even if he did it, it was justified. And I think the defense knows this, and they know that more attention creates the possibility of jury nullification, or maybe even an acquittal."
PALISADES FIRE DEADLOCK FUELS FEAR THAT IDEOLOGY IS CREEPING INTO JURY BOX — AND MANGIONE COULD BE NEXT
Luigi Mangione appears at a pre-trial hearing in Manhattan Criminal Court in New York, NY, Wednesday, June 17, 2026. (Pool via Barry Williams for New York Daily News)
Rahmani said the defense is counting on influencers to do what a courtroom sketch never could: keep the case viral.

"Obviously, those handwritten sketches, they're not as interesting as clips that you can post on TikTok or Instagram reels. The defense knows this and they want to take advantage of that influencer content and those viral videos," Rahmani said.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Rahmani's argument tracks with the behavior of Mangione's supporters, who have lined up outside federal and state courthouses for a chance to see the man accused of killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. One woman, Ashley, part of a group calling itself "The Mangionistas," told the New York Post she camped outside the court in December, and said it wasn't her first time.
SEND US A TIP
Luigi Mangione appears at an evidence suppression hearing at the Manhattan Supreme Court in New York City, U.S., May 18, 2026. (Jeenah Moon/Reuters via Pool)
"I froze my a-- off last time so I brought a heater, a tent, everything,’’ another individual said.
GOT A TIP?
Rahmani said the strategy by Mangione's attorneys is to hopefully get enough influencers talking about the case to the point where it impacts jurors.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"Jurors are supposed to decide the case solely based on the facts and evidence in the case, and they certainly shouldn't be on social media or AI or Google getting information about the case. But jurors are ordinary people, and they can't help but be influenced by these outside voices," he said. "And the defense knows this, and they know that more media attention likely means pressure on the jurors or potentially people that may be stealth jurors that may want to get on the panel to actually free Luigi in this case."
MANHATTAN DA'S OFFICE SAYS LUIGI MANGIONE DEFENSE SPREAD FALSE CLAIMS ABOUT MURDER TRIAL MEDIA PLAN

Luigi Mangione supporter outside of his hearing in New York Supreme Criminal Court, in New York, NY, May 18, 2026. Mangione is accused of murdering UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. (John Taggart for Fox News Digital)
While Rahmani said it's clear what the defense is trying to do, their entire argument for getting the trial livestreamed is a stunt because New York state law prohibits it.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"There's no world where the defense is gonna get its request unless New York law changes or the judge does something extraordinary," Rahmani said. "People will think that there's some sort of cover-up because they've seen other high-profile trials livestreamed and they think that people may think that Luigi Mangione is not getting a fair trial because there's a lack of transparency."
Fox News Digital reached out to Mangione's attorneys for comment.

title: Marine veteran Las Vegas officer killed in shooting; armed suspect also dead
summary: A Las Vegas police officer and Marine veteran was fatally shot responding to a suspected gunman waving a firearm at a business on East Tropicana Avenue.
story: A Las Vegas police officer was killed while responding to a report of a suspected gunman, who was also killed in the exchange. (via Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department)
A Las Vegas police officer who was a Marine veteran was killed Tuesday while responding to a report of an armed person, authorities said. The suspect was also killed in the encounter.

Officers and police drones were sent to a business in the 4500 block of East Tropicana Avenue shortly before 4 p.m. after a caller reported that a person was waving a firearm and appeared to be intoxicated, according to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department.
MULTIPLE PEOPLE KILLED IN SHOOTING AT IDAHO IN-N-OUT RESTAURANT, SUSPECT DEAD
Sheriff Kevin McMahill said an officer was wounded in the shooting and rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. (Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department)
Police said officers located the armed suspect near Mountain Vista Street and the Interstate 11 underpass. The suspect then opened fire on the officers, prompting at least one officer to return fire.
The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene.
A 30-year-old officer was wounded during the exchange and taken to University Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead, Clark County Sheriff Kevin McMahill said during a news briefing.

"A 30-year-old Las Vegas police officer was then worked on heroically by the Clark County Fire Department, other officers and EMS," McMahill said. "He was transported to UMC where nurses worked to save his life."
DEPUTY US MARSHAL FATALLY SHOT WHILE SERVING ARREST WARRANT IN LOUISIANA
The sheriff said the officer was a Marine veteran who had worked for the police department since November 2023. (Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department)
"Unfortunately, our officer has passed," the sheriff continued.
McMahill said the officer was a Marine veteran who had served with the police department since November 2023.
"A person who served this country and this community," McMahill said. "As you can imagine, I have lots of grieving police officers and a grieving community."
The police department offered its condolences to the officer’s family and pledged to support them "in every way we can in the days ahead."
The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene. (Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department)
Other law enforcement agencies also mourned the officer’s death.

"The Nevada State Police extends our heartfelt condolences to the family, friends and loved ones of the fallen officer, and to our partners at the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department," the agency said in a Facebook statement. "Our thoughts are with you during this difficult time."

title: Lindsay Clancy strikes evidence deal as fingerprint gap opens trial debate, expert says
summary: Lindsay Clancy agreed to a stipulation in court as a state police trooper testified no usable fingerprints were found on a knife or exercise bands.
story: Lindsay Clancy told a Massachusetts judge she knowingly and voluntarily agreed to a set of stipulated facts, relieving prosecutors of the burden of proving those facts at her murder trial.

Lindsay Clancy spoke directly in court Tuesday, repeatedly answering, "Yes, Your Honor," as she agreed to let prosecutors treat certain forensic facts as established hours before a state police trooper testified that investigators recovered no usable fingerprints from a knife or three exercise bands.

The developments narrowed the Massachusetts mother’s murder trial toward its central dispute: whether Clancy was criminally responsible when her three children were killed inside the family’s Duxbury home.
Before jurors entered the courtroom, Judge William Sullivan questioned Clancy about a stipulation covering certain evidence.
HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

"You understand that by signing the stipulation, you’re agreeing that the Commonwealth does not have to prove these certain facts that are contained in the stipulation," Sullivan said. "Do you understand that?"
"Yes, Your Honor," Clancy replied.
Defendant Lindsay Clancy listens during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday, July 30, 2026. (CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP, Pool)
Asked whether anyone had forced or threatened her to accept the agreement, Clancy said, "No, Your Honor."
Sullivan found that Clancy was competent and had entered the stipulation "knowingly, intelligently, voluntarily and willingly."
LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS PILL USE AS EXPERT SAYS EVIDENCE COULD SHAPE MURDER TRIAL

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington said the agreement would prevent prosecutors from calling dozens of witnesses solely to establish the chain of custody for blood, bodily fluids, exercise bands and DNA evidence.
"We have not been contesting the government’s case in chief, if you will," Reddington said.
The stipulation is not a guilty plea or an admission that Clancy was criminally responsible for the deaths of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.
WATCH: Former prosecutor explains strategy behind Lindsay Clancy evidence agreement

Margaret McLean, a former criminal prosecutor and trial attorney who teaches law at Boston College’s Carroll School of Management, said the agreement allows the defense to steer jurors away from repetitive forensic testimony and toward Clancy’s mental state.
LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN

"The legal strategy behind the move by the defense is to steer the jury’s focus away from the horrific nature of the acts and to that central issue of criminal intent, or what we would call mens rea," McLean told Fox News Digital.
McLean said Clancy’s measured responses Tuesday should not be taken as evidence of her mental condition on Jan. 24, 2023.

"She sounded rational. She understands what she’s doing," McLean said. "But remember, the Commonwealth’s burden of proof is to prove that she was sane beyond a reasonable doubt at the time the crimes were committed -- not today, not two weeks ago."
WATCH: Trooper details crime scene evidence collection at Lindsey Clancy's home
Later, Massachusetts State Police Trooper Jonathan O’Loughlin testified about examining a knife and three exercise bands collected from the home.
HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL
O’Loughlin said the knife contained an area of friction-ridge impression, but investigators could not use it to identify anyone.
"There was not enough characteristics or minutia to do any comparison," O’Loughlin said, adding that the impression had "no value."

Defendant Lindsay Clancy on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, the fifth day of testimony at Plymouth Superior Court for her murder trial. Clancy is charged with three counts of murder in connection with the death of her three young children in 2023 at their Duxbury home. Clancy says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and is not criminally responsible. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
The yellow, black and blue exercise bands similarly produced no impressions suitable for comparison.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
"The bottom line is that you didn’t get any fingerprints," Reddington said.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
"Correct," O’Loughlin replied.
SEND US A TIP
Lindsay Clancy's three children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. (Lindsay Marie Clancy facebook)
GOT A TIP?
O’Loughlin said fingerprints are "very, very, very fragile" and can be affected by an object’s texture, environmental conditions, movement, grip strength or whether a surface was wiped.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
McLean said the absence of identifiable prints could make jurors wonder whether gloves were used or the items were wiped, potentially viewing the missing prints as evidence of planning.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
The defense, she said, can counter that jurors must not "speculate on something that’s not in evidence."

"They can use their common sense when they go to the table and they deliberate," McLean said, "but they can’t speculate [about] things that are not in the evidence."

title: Mom of 4 recovering after suspected spider bite leads to severe complications: reports
summary: Britagne Miller reportedly spent weeks hospitalized, including time in intensive care, after a suspected spider bite was followed by surgery and infections.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A Kansas mother of four is reportedly recovering after a suspected spider bite led to surgery, serious infections and a weeks-long hospital stay.

Britagne Miller of Goddard — about 14 miles west of Wichita — said she was sitting around a campfire with her husband and children at Cheney Lake May 28, when several spiders crawled on her and apparently bit her, according to local outlets KAKE and FOX Kansas.
Four days later, the area around one bite on her calf became swollen and painful, prompting her to seek medical care, FOX Kansas reported.
"This one kept swelling and swelling, and it was like, you know, a fire stir that's metal," Miller told KAKE. "It was like shooting down my leg into my foot, and it felt like it was being stabbed."
GIANT GOLDEN SPIDERS COULD SPREAD THIS SUMMER; EXPERTS DOWNPLAY HEALTH RISK
Britagne Miller said she was sitting around a campfire with her husband and children May 28 when several spiders crawled on her and apparently bit her. (Jake Miller via GoFundMe)

Miller, who chose to continue treatment rather than enter hospice care, said she remembers little from her time in intensive care, according to the outlet.

Britagne Miller said she remembers little from her time in intensive care. (Jake Miller via GoFundMe)

Miller now requires home health care, physical therapy and regular visits with specialists. She also hopes to receive a liver transplant but is not yet eligible to be placed on the transplant list, according to KAKE and the GoFundMe.
Doctors have not confirmed what kind of spider bit her, KAKE reported.
Dr. Raymond Cloyd, a horticultural entomologist at Kansas State University, told KAKE the brown recluse and black widow are two venomous spiders commonly found in Kansas.

title: Man arrested at Trump golf course ahead of president’s visit allegedly had weapons cache
summary: A man allegedly photographing security preparations at Trump National Golf Club was found with weapons, body armor and concerning notebooks.
story: Fox News senior national correspondent Kevin Corke reports on the details surrounding the arrest of an armed suspect at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, Calif., on 'Jesse Watters Primetime.'

A California man was arrested Sunday at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes after allegedly monitoring security planning activities days before the president’s visit, and was later found with a cache of weapons and body armor, authorities said.
Jeanine John Taele, 38, of Downey, pleaded not guilty Tuesday to four criminal charges stemming from his arrest outside the golf course days before President Donald Trump's scheduled visit.
Trump arrived in Los Angeles late Tuesday for a Republican National Committee fundraiser.

A Los Angeles County judge set Taele's bail at $250,000, ordered him not to possess any weapons, barred him from Trump National Golf Club and prohibited him from leaving California while the case is pending.
His next court appearance is scheduled for Aug. 26, for a preliminary hearing setting and bail review.
TWO YEARS AFTER BUTLER, THREATS AGAINST TRUMP KEEP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT IN SHARP FOCUS

According to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, the investigation began Sunday, when plainclothes federal agents spotted Taele walking the grounds of Trump National Golf Club while taking photographs and videos and appearing to monitor security-planning activities.

Deputies from the Lomita Sheriff's Station responded around 3:30 p.m. and contacted Taele. During a pat-down, deputies allegedly recovered a 16-round magazine loaded with hollow-point ammunition from Taele's pants pocket.

Authorities then searched his vehicle, which was parked in the golf course parking lot, and recovered a loaded pistol with a round in the chamber, along with another loaded magazine containing hollow-point ammunition.
Jeanine John Taele, 38, pleaded not guilty to four criminal charges stemming from his arrest outside the golf course days before President Donald Trump's scheduled visit. (FBI)
Taele claimed he was employed by the State Department and was at the site for a security detail.

He was initially arrested on suspicion of carrying a concealed firearm and possessing prohibited ammunition. Prosecutors later charged him with receiving a large-capacity magazine, carrying a concealed firearm in a vehicle and possession of a short-barreled rifle or shotgun.
The discovery prompted detectives with the Sheriff's Department's Major Crimes Bureau assigned to the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force to obtain a search warrant for Taele's Downey home.
The entrance to Trump National Golf Club Los Angeles, in Rancho Palos Verdes, Calif. (AP Photo/John Antczak, File)

Investigators said they recovered an illegally modified AR-platform rifle; a 1911 .45-caliber pistol; an AR-platform upper receiver; body armor; high-capacity magazines; bulk pistol and rifle ammunition; two radio signal devices; and multiple notebooks containing what authorities described as "concerning statements."

Separately, prosecutors also charged Taele with second-degree robbery in connection with an alleged Nov. 4, 2025, incident that was already under investigation by the El Segundo Police Department before Sunday's arrest at the golf course.

The investigation is being conducted jointly by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force and the U.S. Secret Service. Officials said additional charges could be filed as the investigation continues.

"With respect to this defendant, we do not comment on the specifics of protective intelligence matters. However, the U.S. Secret Service thoroughly investigates any information or activity that may reasonably be perceived as a protective intelligence concern or indicate a potential threat or directed interest toward any individual under Secret Service protection," the U.S. Secret Service said in a statement.

"We are grateful to our partners at the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department and the Joint Terrorism Task Force for their continued support and strong partnership in advancing our shared investigative and protective missions," it added.
Authorities said they have identified no credible threat to the surrounding community but noted the investigation remains active.

The FBI's Los Angeles Field Office confirmed to Fox News Digital that the bureau's Joint Terrorism Task Force is continuing to investigate the case with the U.S. Secret Service and the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department but declined to comment further because the investigation remains ongoing.
President Donald Trump and Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, Calif.   (Fox News)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A spokesperson for The Trump Organization thanked the agencies involved in the response.

"We are incredibly grateful to the local law enforcement, the United States Secret Service, the FBI, and all supporting agencies for their swift response and dedication to keeping everyone safe," the spokesperson said.
Trump briefly addressed the incident on Tuesday, saying only consequential presidents are targeted.
"Well, the only thing I get a little solace from is, they say only consequential presidents. And I am definitely consequential," he said during an appearance on "Fox News @ Night."

title: More than half of some US weapons stockpiles used in Iran war, raising concerns about China threat
summary: CSIS warns depleted U.S. weapons stockpiles from the Iran war could embolden China as President Xi watches munitions levels amid Taiwan tensions.
story: ‘Special Report’ anchor Bret Baier has the details on the Iran conflict’s impact on the United States' missile defense stockpiles.

Some estimates show the U.S. has used more than half of its stockpiles of some weapons systems in the war with Iran. The Center for Strategic and International Studies found the U.S. has enough missiles to continue fighting in Iran under any plausible scenario, but the group says the true issue with the shrinking stockpiles is future wars.

"We can go on against Iran for quite a long time, even if we've used half the inventory. That means that half the inventories are still available," said Mark Cancian, a retired U.S. Marines colonel and senior advisor with the CSIS Defense and Security Department.
"The risk is about a future conflict in the Western Pacific against China."
Cancian pointed to reports that military officials have grown more concerned over the U.S. weapons inventory when factoring in other possible conflicts, such as one with China.
WEAPONS STOCKPILE SHORTAGES IMPACTING MILITARY STRATEGY IN THE MIDEAST

"The depletion of munitions was a major topic and a major reason for the suspension of air attacks," Cancian said. "Our inventories were getting way below what the war planners wanted. That might encourage China to do something."

Almost one-third of Tomahawk missiles have been used since the war in Iran began. Nearly two-thirds of Patriot missile interceptors have been depleted. Just over half of precision strike missiles remain.
President Donald Trump insists the U.S. has plenty of munitions to continue in Iran.
A rendered image of a Tomahawk missile (Provided to Fox News Digital)
"We have a lot of ammunition, different types," President Trump said in July. "I mean, more than we could ever use, no matter what. But we have a lot. I'd like to have more, to be honest."
HEGSETH DISMISSES ‘FOOLISH’ US STOCKPILE CONCERNS AS IRAN CONFLICT TESTS MUNITIONS
CSIS notes many munition stockpiles are substantial but focused its analysis on seven key weapons that have been effective in Iran and would also be valuable in a possible Pacific conflict.
An Iranian missile is launched during a military exercise in an undisclosed location in Iran Aug. 20, 2025.  (Iranian Army/WANA/Handout via Reuters)

"We have a defense industrial base that needs to be fixed at a very critical time in our history with the conflict in the Middle East," Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Texas, said. "President Xi of China is watching our stockpiles very closely as he contemplates threatening behavior towards the Taiwan straits, and, so, it all kind of factors in together here. And to be a strong United States, we need a strong military and project strength abroad."
The Pentagon is requesting significant increases in spending for weapons manufacturing, and lawmakers from both sides of the aisle believe the funding is of importance.
TRUMP IS PROVING THAT THE WAY TO BETTER OUR MILITARY IS TO SECURE OUR SUPPLY CHAINS

"Look, I have real concerns about our defense industrial base, and God forbid we find ourselves in a lengthy, serious war in our ability to produce what we need," Rep. Chris Deluzio, D-Pa., said. "I actually think it's a place where you can get some cooperation across the parties who want to see us re-industrialize."

The Pentagon’s budget request for fiscal year 2027 includes $5.8 Billion for Tomahawk missiles, an increase of 513% from the fiscal year 2026 request. Proposed spending for precision strike missiles is 245% higher, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAADS) is up 650% and the request for Patriot Missile Segment Enhancement is 927% higher.

"Listen, if it's a $1.5 trillion package for defense, I'm all in. I really am," Rep. Troy Nehls, R-Texas, said. "The munitions are going to be there. We're going continue to do what we have to do to protect the world, protect Israel and everybody else in the region."
U.S. Central Command said it carried out another wave of airstrikes against Iran July 17, 2026. (CENTCOM)
If and when the funding is approved, it could take years for the new munitions to reach the battlefield.

"It takes quite a long time for the U.S. to produce new interceptors. They're complex manufacturing assemblages, and thus depleting those stockpiles does leave the U S materially worse off than it otherwise would have been in the current conflict," said UC Berkeley Senior Research Scholar Cameron Tracy.

The Patriot missiles requested in the fiscal year 2027 budget likely will not be available on the front line for another 3½ years. The Tomahawk estimated delivery time sits at almost four years. Some munitions orders could take as long as five years.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE U.S. NEWS

"Before the war, it would typically take about two years for the first system to arrive and then another year after that for the last," Cancian said. "You have to sign a contract, and then the manufacturer has to go out with the subcontractors and get all the materials. With the war, those timelines have been extended."

The Trump administration has created framework agreements with contractors to increase production capacity for key munitions. The deals call for new facilities, ambitious timelines and additional weapons systems.

"You can increase production capacity — we are doing that — [for] Patriot and many other systems. First, you have to recruit more people and train them up," Cancian said. "Then you can expand your facilities, but that takes time. You got to build the facilities, and you got to get all the permits and everything else. So, it can be done. We're seeing it happen, but, again, it takes time."

story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A Florida family is mourning its 3-year-old daughter after police said she became trapped in a toy kitchen play set while at a babysitter's home.
The girl, identified by loved ones as Briella, died July 27, four days after Boynton Beach police said she was found unresponsive with her head stuck inside the play set.
Officers rushed to the Meadows of Boynton Beach community shortly after 11 a.m. on July 23 after receiving a report of a child who was not breathing.
Police immediately began life-saving measures before Boynton Beach Fire Rescue transported the toddler to a nearby hospital, where she remained in critical condition until her death.
DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED
Briella smiles in a family photo before the tragic incident that claimed the Florida toddler's life. (GoFundMe)
Investigators said the 3-year-old and her sibling were at a babysitter's home when the incident happened.
According to Boynton Beach police, the babysitter had left the residence and placed the children in the care of the babysitter's spouse.
While the children played downstairs, the spouse remained upstairs, periodically checking on them and bringing them snacks, police said.
TENNESSEE WOMAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY TRYING TO DROWN ONE OF HER CHILDREN IN BACKYARD POOL
Briella, the 3-year-old Florida girl who died following a tragic incident at a babysitter's home, is pictured with another child in an undated photo. (GoFundMe)

title: Kentucky child killer walks free as family says justice failed despite years of legal fights
summary: Ronald Exantus walked free after serving his sentence for the 2015 home invasion that killed 6-year-old Logan Tipton despite Logan's Law reforms.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

The Kentucky father whose 6-year-old son was stabbed to death while sleeping says the man found not guilty by reason of insanity in the killing received "a slap on the wrist" after being released from prison July 29 upon completing his sentence for assaulting three surviving family members.

Ronald Exantus was released from Kentucky Department of Corrections custody July 29 after completing the sentence imposed for assaulting Logan Tipton's father and sisters during the 2015 home invasion that left the 6-year-old dead.

The case stunned Kentucky after prosecutors said Exantus broke into the Tipton family's home on Dec. 7, 2015, and fatally stabbed 6-year-old Logan Tipton while he slept. Logan's father and two sisters were also stabbed but survived the attack. A jury later found Exantus not guilty by reason of insanity on murder and burglary charges but guilty but mentally ill on assault charges involving the surviving family members.
The assault convictions resulted in the prison sentence he completed last week, reigniting outrage from the Tipton family and renewed questions about Kentucky's criminal justice system.
FLORIDA AG SEEKS JUDGE'S IMPEACHMENT AFTER BABY DROWNING COVID INSANITY ACQUITTAL
Ronald Exantus served 11 years, nine months and 18 days before he was released July 29.  (Fox News Channel)

"The judge and jury gave this monster a slap on the wrist while handing down a life sentence to my family," Logan's father, Dean Tipton, wrote on Facebook after Exantus' release. "Make sure to lock your doors and keep an eye out for baby killers. He will be released today. Watch your house, your neighbors house, your kids, your neighbors kids. He could be coming to your town. Kentucky justice at its finest."
According to the Kentucky Department of Corrections, Exantus completed the sentence imposed by the court after receiving sentence credits required under Kentucky law.
HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER
A booking photo of Ronald Exantus, who was found not guilty by reason of insanity in the killing of 6-year-old Logan Tipton and later convicted of assault charges. (Kentucy Online Offender Lookup)

"Ronald Exantus has served the sentence issued by the Woodford Circuit Court and has been released," the department told Fox News Digital. "He is no longer in the custody of the Department of Corrections."

Corrections officials emphasized that juries and courts determine an offender's sentence, while the department is responsible for calculating that sentence under Kentucky law, including applying any earned statutory sentence credits.
Once Exantus reached his legally calculated sentence expiration date, the agency said it no longer had authority to keep him incarcerated.
The department also stressed that the Kentucky Parole Board "did not release Exantus, and he was not released early."

Exantus was briefly released on mandatory reentry supervision in October 2025 before moving to Florida, where authorities said he violated the conditions of his supervision by failing to register as a convicted felon.

He was returned to Kentucky after the violation, and the Parole Board revoked his mandatory reentry supervision, ordering him back to prison. The department said he ultimately remained incarcerated until completing his sentence July 29.
NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'
Prosecutors said Ronald Exantus received nearly nine years of sentence credit, as is required under Kentucky law, that accelerated his release. (Woodford County Detention Center)
Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman said his office worked alongside prosecutors, law enforcement and corrections officials to keep Exantus incarcerated for as long as the law allowed.

In a November 2025 letter to the Kentucky Parole Board, Coleman urged board members to revoke Exantus' mandatory reentry supervision after Exantus violated its conditions in Florida and required him to serve the remainder of his sentence in prison.
"The public good and common sense demand nothing less," Coleman wrote, calling Logan Tipton's killing "every parent's worst nightmare."
The Parole Board ultimately revoked Exantus' mandatory reentry supervision and ordered him back to prison after finding he violated the terms of his supervision.

Ahead of Exantus' scheduled release, the Kentucky Justice and Public Safety Cabinet also notified the trial judge, Commonwealth's Attorney Kelli Kearney and defense counsel that they could pursue involuntary hospitalization proceedings before his sentence expired if they believed it was appropriate under Kentucky law.
The Department of Corrections said it lacked the legal authority to continue holding Exantus once he completed his sentence unless another lawful basis for detention was established.
In a November 2025 interview with WKYT, Coleman said "the system failed the Tipton family," while pledging to pursue every legal avenue available to keep Exantus incarcerated.
CALIFORNIA MOM RIPS NEWSOM-BACKED 'DIVERSION PROGRAM' THAT APPEARS TO BENEFIT HER SON'S KILLER
Undated photo of Logan Tipton (GoFundMe)
Public outrage over Logan’s case helped spur Kentucky lawmakers to pass House Bill 422, known as Logan’s Law, which Gov. Andy Beshear signed in April.

The law revised Kentucky’s insanity defense and mandatory reentry supervision rules in response to issues raised by Exantus’ case. But because it does not apply retroactively, it had no effect on Exantus' sentence or July 29 release.
State Rep. Daniel Fister, who helped champion the legislation, called Exantus' release "heartbreaking" and vowed to continue working with the Tipton family to strengthen Kentucky's criminal laws.
"My heart breaks yet again for the Tipton family and our community as we are once again forced to endure the pain and uncertainty caused by Ronald Exantus," Fister told Fox News Digital.
NORTH CAROLINA TEACHER'S KILLING REIGNITES SCRUTINY OF ROY COOPER'S CRIMINAL JUSTICE RECORD IN SENATE RACE
Dean Tipton stands alongside Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear and others after signing House Bill 422, known as Logan's Law. (Dean Tipton Facebook)
"No family should have to endure this kind of trauma, and every Kentuckian deserves confidence that our justice system will protect innocent victims and hold violent offenders accountable."
Fister said Logan's Law was "an important step forward" but promised lawmakers would continue pursuing reforms to better protect Kentucky families.
"We owe it to Logan's memory and to every family across the Commonwealth to continue pursuing reforms that put the safety of innocent Kentuckians first," he said.

Fister also said Exantus' release underscores broader concerns about Kentucky's criminal justice system, arguing that delays in implementing provisions of House Bill 5 have allowed some violent offenders to become eligible for parole earlier than lawmakers intended.
DEVASTATED MOTHER BLAMES SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICIES AFTER CAREER CRIMINAL IS CHARGED IN SON’S DEATH
"That is deeply troubling for victims and their families who deserve confidence that violent criminals will be held fully accountable," he said.
State Rep. T.J. Roberts, who also helped author Logan's Law, called Exantus' release "a gross miscarriage of justice."

"Once again, Kentucky's judiciary has failed the Tipton family," Roberts told Fox News Digital. "The monster who killed Logan Tipton should spend the rest of his life in prison, at a minimum, and his release is a gross miscarriage of justice. The Tipton family, all of Kentucky, and all of America deserve so much better than what this government offers to the innocent."
Roberts noted that the U.S. Constitution prohibits lawmakers from retroactively increasing criminal penalties, meaning Logan's Law could not be applied to Exantus after his conviction.
GIANNO CALDWELL: FOUR YEARS AFTER MY BROTHER’S MURDER, I’M MARCHING FOR JUSTICE
Logan Tipton in his football uniform (Dean Tipton Facebook)

Calling Logan's Law "a great first step," Roberts said he plans to introduce additional legislation that would expand the availability of life without parole for murder convictions, strengthen victim notification requirements and further protect Kentuckians from violent offenders.
"I intend to file legislation to ensure our justice system protects the innocent, not violent offenders," he said.
Roberts also offered a message directly to the Tipton family.
"I want the Tipton family to know they have my support and the support of millions of people who have heard their story," he said. "God is with them, and we will not let Logan's life be forgotten."
BODYCAM FOOTAGE FUELS BACKLASH AFTER POLICE HANDCUFF DYING STABBING VICTIM
For Tipton, Exantus' release reopened wounds that have never healed.
"Knowing that this monster gets to walk free and live his life, while I lay in this bed and my baby boy is in the grave," he wrote. "This may be my breaking point."
Although Logan's Law has now taken effect, Tipton said he believes Kentucky must go further.
"So I've come to terms that even though we got Logans Law passed it is still not enough," he wrote. "Violent criminals should not be able to knock so much time off their sentence.
"Our judicial system as a whole needs to be over hauled and I am gonna fight for more change."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Despite helping inspire Logan's Law, the Tipton family says its fight is far from over. The family has launched a GoFundMe to help pay for attorneys as they pursue additional legal remedies and continue pushing for further criminal justice reforms.

"We turned our deepest grief into a fierce, relentless battle to change the law so no other family would ever have to suffer the way we have," the family wrote on the fundraising page. But while Logan's Law was signed this year, they noted it "does not retroactively stop our son's killer from being released."
"The fight is not over and we need your help," the family added.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Air Force says two advanced stealthy aircraft are ahead of schedule, with first delivery set for 2027
summary: The B-21 Raider stealth bomber program accelerated 25% after a $4.5 billion funding boost, with Northrop Grumman targeting seven bombers annually.
story: Bill Hemmer and John Spencer, executive director of the Urban Warfare Institute, discuss the Pentagon's new initiative to oversee military drones and autonomous systems. Spencer emphasizes the necessity for the U.S. to lead in drone technology, citing lessons from the Ukraine war and the significant budget requested for research and development.

The Air Force says its next-generation B-21 Raider stealth bomber program is ahead of schedule, with the first operational aircraft expected to arrive at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in 2027.

The service's sixth-generation F-47 fighter is also progressing faster than expected, according to Gen. Dale White, director of Critical Major Weapon Systems, who discussed both programs during the Air Force's Life Cycle Industry Days conference in Dayton, Ohio.
White said the B-21 acquisition program has accelerated by roughly 25% since a one-time $4.5 billion funding boost was included in the 2025 reconciliation bill.
The comments provide one of the clearest public updates yet on the status of the Air Force's two flagship next-generation aircraft programs.
AMERICA’S NEW STEALTH B-21 RAIDER TAKES NEXT STEP WITH SECOND BOMBER’S FIRST FLIGHT
A B-21 takes flight near Edwards Air Force base in September 2025. (Air Force)

The update comes months after the Air Force announced a second B-21 Raider joined flight testing at Edwards Air Force Base in California, a milestone officials at the time said would accelerate testing and weapons integration for America's first new long-range bomber in more than three decades.

White said the first operational B-21 is expected to be "on the ramp" at Ellsworth in 2027, with Northrop Grumman planning to eventually produce seven operational bombers annually. The Pentagon has requested $6.1 billion for the B-21 program in its fiscal year 2027 budget proposal.

Built by Northrop Grumman, the B-21 is designed to carry both conventional and nuclear weapons while penetrating advanced enemy air defenses. The aircraft is expected to eventually replace the B-1 Lancer and B-2 Spirit while operating alongside modernized B-52 Stratofortress bombers expected to remain in service into the middle of the century. The Air Force plans to acquire at least 100 B-21 bombers.
White also said planning for the Boeing-built F-47 has reached an "unprecedented maturity."
INSIDE AMERICA’S 6TH-GEN ARSENAL: B-21, F-47, AND THE FUTURE OF AIR DOMINANCE
The crew at a test flight of a B-21. (Air Force)

The Air Force plans to acquire 185 F-47 fighters, with the first flight scheduled for 2028. The aircraft will replace the F-22 Raptor as the service's primary air superiority fighter and is expected to operate alongside Collaborative Combat Aircraft, autonomous "loyal wingman" drones designed to support crewed aircraft in combat. The Pentagon has requested $5.03 billion for the F-47 program in its fiscal year 2027 budget request.

The man accused of setting the largest of the wildfires that have destroyed hundreds of buildings and forced tens of thousands of people from their homes in eastern Washington was previously charged with first-degree murder before pleading guilty to a reduced manslaughter charge, court records show.

Aaron F. Farinacci, 37, was arrested Monday on suspicion of first-degree arson in connection with the Old Trails Fire, the largest of three blazes burning in and around Spokane, Washington's second-largest city.

The fires have destroyed at least 700 buildings and forced about 67,000 people to evacuate. Authorities have not alleged any connection between Farinacci and the other two fires, which remain under investigation.

Detectives obtained arrest and search warrants before taking Farinacci into custody without incident at his Spokane residence, where he was booked into the Spokane County Jail on suspicion of first-degree arson.

title: Washington man arrested on arson charge tied to devastating Spokane wildfire
summary: A man was arrested and charged with arson on Monday in connection with the Old Trails Fire in the Spokane area in Washington state, police said.
story: Fox News’ Sarah Alegre reports on wildfires across Spokane County, Washington, destroying hundreds of structures and forcing thousands of residents to evacuate on ‘Special Report.’

A Washington state man was arrested Monday on a first-degree arson charge in connection with the Old Trails Fire, one of several wildfires that have destroyed hundreds of structures and forced tens of thousands of people to evacuate the Spokane area, authorities said.

Aaron F. Farinacci, 37, was taken into custody after Spokane County Sheriff’s Office detectives and Washington Department of Natural Resources investigators developed probable cause to arrest him, according to the sheriff’s office.

Citizen tips and information from Airway Heights police officers and Spokane County sheriff’s deputies who responded to the initial call and conducted evacuations helped lead investigators to Farinacci, the sheriff’s office said.
Authorities described Farinacci as a convicted felon from Arizona but said they had found no documented criminal history involving fires.
Investigators have not connected Farinacci to the two other major blazes burning in the area, the Autumn Lane and Fairview fires, officials said.

"We will be looking into any other crimes Mr. Farinacci may have committed in the past," Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said during a news briefing.
Nowels said first-degree arson was the charge supported by probable cause at that stage of the investigation and cautioned that the case could change as authorities gathered additional evidence.
Detectives obtained an arrest warrant for Farinacci and a search warrant for his residence in the 2800 block of West Elliott Drive, according to the sheriff’s office.
Deputies served the warrant Monday and arrested Farinacci without incident. Authorities said detectives found a butane lighter and waterproof matches while detaining and searching him.

The Old Trails Fire was first reported Saturday near North Old Trails Road and West Euclid Road. It became the largest of three destructive fires burning around Spokane and remained uncontained Monday, according to authorities and wire reports.

The three fires had collectively destroyed at least 700 structures and prompted evacuation orders affecting approximately 67,000 people as of Monday, according to The Associated Press. More than 1,000 firefighters were battling the blazes.

title: Pennsylvania school bus aide accused of sexually assaulting special needs teen
summary: A Pennsylvania bus aide faces indecent assault and child endangerment charges after allegedly inappropriately touching a special needs student.
story: The father of the Georgia school shooter, Colin Gray, is sentenced to 15 years in prison. Legal analyst Donna Rotunno joins 'Fox & Friends First' to discuss the historic sentencing precedent and parental responsibility.

A Pennsylvania school bus aide was arrested after he allegedly inappropriately touched a 14-year-old girl with special needs and appeared to take photographs and videos of her with his cellphone, according to police.
Ali Khan, 62, was charged with endangering the welfare of a child, corruption of minors, indecent assault and related offenses, the Bensalem Township Police Department said.
Khan was being held at the Bucks County Correctional Facility after failing to post 10% of his $500,000 bail.
The girl’s parents contacted police on Thursday, July 30, to report that their daughter had allegedly been inappropriately touched by a bus aide earlier that day, according to investigators.
HIGH SCHOOL COUNSELOR PLEADS GUILTY TO MULTIPLE SEX CRIMES INVOLVING TEEN SHE WAS MEANT TO HELP
Ali Khan, 62, was arrested for inappropriately touching a special needs teenager. (Bensalem Township Police)

Police said their investigation determined that Khan allegedly touched the Bensalem High School student multiple times on Wednesday, July 29, and Thursday, July 30, while she was riding a bus to the school’s extended school year program.

Investigators said surveillance footage from inside the bus showed Khan directing the girl to a specific seat before allegedly touching her inappropriately while securing her seatbelt and after she was seated.
Police said the footage also appeared to show Khan engaging in sexual conduct and using a cellphone to photograph or record the girl.
Ali Khan was charged with endangering the welfare of a child, corruption of minors and indecent assault. (Google Maps)

"Bensalem Police would like to commend the victim of this assault for having the courage to come forward and report the assault," police said. "Additionally, Bensalem Police would like to thank the Bensalem School District for their assistance with this investigation. The safety and well-being of our students continues to be the top priority of both the Bensalem Township Police Department and the Bensalem School District."
The Bensalem Township School District said the employee was immediately removed from service and from the district pending the outcome of criminal and administrative investigations.

"The safety and well-being of our students is our highest priority," the district said in a statement. "Whenever concerns involving student safety are brought to our attention, we act immediately to protect students, support families, and cooperate fully with law enforcement. We are committed to conducting a thorough administrative review while respecting the integrity of the criminal investigation."
CALIFORNIA MIDDLE SCHOOL ASSISTANT PRINCIPAL NABBED IN CHILD SEX STING
The footage showed Ali Khan putting his hand inside his pants and touching himself during the encounter. (Bensalem Township Police)

"The district is fully cooperating with the Bensalem Township Police Department and will continue to assist law enforcement as requested. The district will also continue its own administrative investigation in accordance with Board policy, district procedures, and applicable law," the statement added.
Khan’s preliminary hearing is scheduled for Aug. 11, 2026.
The incident remains under investigation.

title: Lindsay Clancy makes courtroom deal that puts mental state at center stage of murder trial
summary: A hospital psychiatrist agreed that Lindsay Clancy could plan and communicate while psychotic, a key concession in the Duxbury murder trial.
story: Lindsay Clancy told a Massachusetts judge she knowingly and voluntarily agreed to a set of stipulated facts, relieving prosecutors of the burden of proving those facts at her murder trial.
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, contact the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Lindsay Clancy agreed Tuesday to allow prosecutors to treat certain forensic facts as established, narrowing the Massachusetts mother’s murder trial toward the central question of whether she was criminally responsible for the murders of her three children.

Clancy repeatedly answered, "Yes, your Honor," as Judge William Sullivan explained that the stipulation meant prosecutors would not have to independently prove the listed facts and that she was giving up limited rights to confront witnesses or present evidence contesting them.
Sullivan found that Clancy was competent to enter the agreement and had done so "knowingly, intelligently, voluntarily and willingly."
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington said the agreement would spare jurors days of testimony establishing the chain of custody for blood, bodily fluids and DNA evidence.
HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL
The defense is expected to argue Clancy lacks criminal responsibility because she suffered from postpartum psychosis and was overmedicated. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)
"We have not been contesting the government’s case in chief, if you will," Reddington told the court.
The stipulation is not a guilty plea or an admission that Clancy was legally responsible for murder.

Clancy is charged in the deaths of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, inside the family’s Duxbury home. Her defense says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argue she acted deliberately and understood what she was doing.
Jurors also heard Tuesday from the trauma surgeon who treated Clancy after she fell approximately 20 feet from a second-story window.

Dr. Cristina Carpio testified that Clancy arrived at South Shore Hospital as a Level 1 trauma patient with a body temperature of approximately 82.1 degrees and complex, unstable fractures in her thoracic spine.
Clancy was intubated and later transferred to Brigham and Women’s Hospital for a higher level of care.
WATCH: Trooper reveals what investigators found inside Lindsay Clancy home

A Massachusetts State Police lieutenant later testified that investigators searching the Clancy home found a CVS bag containing a bottle of Pedia-Lax, a larger paper bag with a receipt and multiple medication bottles in an upper kitchen cabinet.
The CVS evidence corroborates her then-husband Patrick Clancy’s account that he left the home to purchase medicine before picking up dinner.
WATCH: Trooper details crime scene evidence collection at Lindsey Clancy's home

Massachusetts State Police forensic scientist Maureen Hartnett testified that she observed "red-brown stains" on Clancy’s hands at South Shore Hospital and collected samples for "potential biological evidence," later taking swabs from beneath her fingernails at Brigham and Women’s Hospital.

"I was informed that additional testing was being requested on some of the red-brown stains that were noted on the exterior of the house, up on the shingles they had not previously collected from," she said.
Hartnett’s testimony established how investigators mapped and preserved biological evidence from Clancy’s body as well as the area where the Massachusetts' mother fell following her suicide attempt.
WATCH: Trooper details specialized crime scene training in Lindsay Clancy trial
Massachusetts State Police Trooper Jonathan O’Loughlin testified that investigators recovered no usable fingerprints from the knife or three exercise bands collected inside the Clancy home.
"Fingerprints are extremely fragile," O’Loughlin said, explaining that investigators processed the items before biological testing because later handling could destroy latent prints.
He said the knife showed limited friction-ridge detail, but there was "not enough characteristics or minutia to do any comparison," and the prints were deemed to have no value.

Defendant Lindsay Clancy on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, the fifth day of testimony at Plymouth Superior Court for her murder trial. Clancy is charged with three counts of murder in connection with the death of her three young children in 2023 at their Duxbury home. Clancy says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and is not criminally responsible. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
Tuesday’s evidence followed Reddington’s effort Monday to blunt prosecutors’ portrayal of Clancy as organized and calculating.
"People can communicate and plan and act on plans even if they’re in the middle of a psychosis, right?" Reddington asked Dr. Sejal Shah Monday.
"Yes," Shah replied.

Reddington then asked whether someone must be "drooling and stumbling and unable to walk and talk" to be psychotic. Shah said no and agreed that a person in psychosis can still communicate with others.

Clancy is charged in the deaths of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, inside the family’s Duxbury home. Her defense maintains she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argue she acted deliberately and understood what she was doing.
LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS ‘BIG SPIRAL’ AS EXPERT SAYS ONE PART ‘SCARED ME’ IN MOM’S MURDER TRIAL
Dr. Sejal Shah testified she examined Clancy multiple times at Boston’s Brigham and Women’s Hospital in January and February 2023. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)

Seth J. Zuckerman, a celebrity criminal defense attorney, former New York City prosecutor and founder of Zuckerman Legal Group, said the case will turn on Clancy’s mental state at the precise time the children were killed.
"What was in her mind at the exact time that she killed her children?" Zuckerman told Fox News Digital.
He said prosecutors have focused on Patrick Clancy’s trips to CVS and a local restaurant, along with his communications with his wife, to portray her as lucid during the critical time frame.
WATCH: Psychiatrist calls Lindsay Clancy an 'honest' patient
LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS PILL USE AS EXPERT SAYS EVIDENCE COULD SHAPE MURDER TRIAL
Shah, an associate chief of psychiatry and medicine at Brigham and Women’s Hospital, first evaluated Clancy five days after the killings.
She testified that Clancy was confused, made mistakes during a cognitive assessment and had experienced visual hallucinations after spinal surgery.
Shah diagnosed delirium and said possible causes included anesthesia, oxygen problems and an elevated heart rate. The symptoms resolved by the following day, Shah said.

Prosecutors argued in opening statements that Lindsay Clancy "deliberately and meticulously" killed her children and "acted intentionally, rationally and swiftly to accomplish a very specific goal." (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
During later evaluations, Clancy appeared calm and cooperative, displayed organized and goal-directed thinking and denied hallucinations and suicidal or homicidal intent.
Reddington used cross-examination to argue those observations did not establish Clancy was free of psychosis at the time of the killings.
"Was she, in your opinion and your experience, an honest patient telling you what her symptoms were, if any?" Reddington asked.
"Yes," Shah said.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"She didn’t go off and try to exaggerate to you and say, ‘I’m seeing visions, and I’m hearing voices,’ and suicidal ideation and homicidal ideas," Reddington said. "She didn’t say any of those things to you, did she?"
"Correct," Shah said.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
"So this is not, in your opinion, someone who was trying to exaggerate her conditions for some legal reason, correct?" Reddington asked.
"No," Shah replied.

Zuckerman called that concession "extremely helpful to the defense," although not decisive.
"They want to portray her as someone who wasn’t manipulative, who didn’t have some grand plan," he said.
Lindsay Clancy appears in court Monday in Plymouth, Massachusetts. She has pleaded not guilty to three counts of murder for the killings of her children. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
SEND US A TIP
On redirect, prosecutors challenged the defense’s portrayal by focusing on Clancy’s medication history.
Shah agreed Clancy was not taking every psychiatric medication discussed at the same time and said she had not known some prescriptions were barely used or untouched.
GOT A TIP?

Shah also confirmed that Clancy requested do-not-resuscitate status after surviving her fall from a second-story window. The hospital did not immediately change her status because of the reported suicide attempt.
Shah said Clancy later agreed her mental health should be stabilized before reconsidering the request.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Zuckerman said Monday’s cross-examination helped the defense by supplying testimony that Clancy could appear lucid at some moments while experiencing severe psychiatric symptoms at others.
Still, he said its value will depend on whether the defense can connect those symptoms to the moment the children were killed.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

"The burden is on the prosecutors to show that she was criminally responsible at the time of the deaths," Zuckerman said. "That is unique to Massachusetts, and I think it’s beneficial to the defense here."

On January 24, 2023, Clancy fatally strangled her three children in the basement of their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home using exercise resistance bands. She then cut her wrists and neck and jumped from a second-story window in a suicide attempt, leaving her partially paralyzed. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)

Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital, has pleaded not guilty to three counts each of murder and strangulation. Judge William Sullivan told jurors that the Commonwealth must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Clancy was criminally responsible when the children were killed.

title: California mom begged for help before ex gunned her down in front of their 4-year-old son: DA
summary: Jeffery Kendall was sentenced to 50 years to life for fatally shooting Brittany Ligdis during a 911 call as their 4-year-old son watched in Pinole.
story: More than two years after prosecutors said Jeffery Kendall fatally shot Brittany Ligdis in front of their 4-year-old son, a judge sentenced him to 50 years to life. Credit: KTVU

More than two years after a California mother's desperate 911 call ended with her 4-year-old son witnessing her killing, the father prosecutors said carried out the execution will spend decades behind bars.

Jeffery Kendall, 39, was sentenced Monday to 50 years to life in prison for murdering 30-year-old Brittany Elizabeth Ligdis just 10 days after she ended their relationship, according to the Contra Costa County District Attorney’s Office.
A jury found Kendall guilty in May of first-degree murder and child endangerment for placing the couple’s young son in a situation that threatened his safety.
DISPATCHER HEARD 'LOUD BANG' BEFORE TIKTOK INFLUENCER WHO OUTED ALLEGED PEDOPHILE HUSBAND FOUND DEAD: AUDIO
File photo of Jeffery Kendall. (KTVU)
Prosecutors said Ligdis called 911 on the morning of Feb. 16, 2024, after Kendall broke into her Pinole home while she hid in a laundry room with their 4-year-old son.
About 90 seconds into the call, Kendall entered the room.
"Let go of me," Ligdis pleaded, according to the district attorney’s office. "You're scaring him."
DECADES-OLD COLD CASE BREAKTHROUGH LEADS TO ARREST IN EXECUTION-STYLE KILLINGS OF MARRIED COUPLE BEFORE CHILD
Law enforcement officers place Jeffery Kendall in handcuffs following his arrest in Santa Cruz, California. (California Highway Patrol)
Moments later, she screamed, "Stop it," before Kendall shot her in the head, prosecutors said.
The couple’s son cried out, "Momma," and fled the room while Kendall ran from the home. Responding officers found Ligdis dead from a gunshot wound to the head.

Deputy District Attorney Tylyn Wells described the killing as "an execution in front of a 4-year-old child" and argued it was not the result of "a mental break," according to the district attorney’s office.
ALABAMA MOTHER SENTENCED TO LIFE FOR HIRING HITMAN TO KILL HER CHILD'S FATHER OVER CUSTODY DISPUTE
A law enforcement officer escorts Jeffery Kendall through a police facility after his arrest. (California Highway Patrol via FOX 2 San Francisco)
Instead, Wells said the murder reflected a pattern often seen in domestic violence cases, where the danger escalates after a victim decides to leave.
Wells asked the court to impose a sentencing enhancement that increased Kendall’s punishment to 50 years to life.
Contra Costa County Superior Court Judge Glenn Kim called the case "one of the most difficult" he had experienced before imposing two consecutive terms of 25 years to life.
Kim also barred Kendall from contacting his son, with limited exceptions subject to court approval, until November 2035, when the boy turns 16.
Separately, Judge Kim convicted Kendall of illegally possessing a 3D-printed semi-automatic pistol and determined that multiple factors supported a harsher sentence.
One year after Brittany Ligdis' death, her mother shared an emotional video urging family and friends to remember her daughter's life rather than the violence that ended it.
Brittany Ligdis smiles while holding her young son in a family photograph taken before her death. (KTVU)

"I want this to be a day to remember Brittany, to memorialize her, the amazing person she was," she said. "Think of her — all the things we miss about her, her kiss, her hug. I'll miss everything myself. I will love her forever."
Kendall remains in county jail awaiting transfer to the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation.
